In Hilbert Space, All Things Are Quantumly Possible

By
Charlie Wood

August 26, 2026

To explore quantum phenomena, we must leave the familiar world and enter the abstract realm of Hilbert space.

At the heart of quantum mechanics lie a few sacred rules for how to use the theory. First and foremost is, roughly, that thou shalt not think about ordinary objects presently whizzing through ordinary space. Rather, quantum mechanics predicts — in exquisite detail — all the possible ways that an object might turn out to be in the future. Exploring those possible futures requires tracking an entirely different mathematical object — an arrow known as a vector, one oriented in an expansive, alien domain.

These arrows aren’t pointing at locations. “It’s a much more abstract space than that,” said Lucien Hardy, a physicist at the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics in Waterloo, Canada. They’re “really pointing in a direction in a possibility space.”

This possibility space is called Hilbert space, and it acts as the primary arena for quantum physics.

The early quantum pioneers didn’t realize — at first — that the arcane math that strikingly captured the conduct of atoms had left the real world behind. It took a visionary mathematical physicist, John von Neumann, to recognize and define the quantum world as a Hilbert space. Once he did, exploring the ins and outs of Hilbert space would lead physicists to a deeper, more unified understanding of quantum physics.

Here’s how von Neumann’s first commandment of quantum physics came to be, and how to understand it.

What Is Hilbert Space?

Von Neumann’s commandments, or axioms, were his way of making sense of the two distinct forms of quantum mechanics developed back-to-back in the 1920s. First came Werner Heisenberg’s “matrix mechanics” in 1925. It used inscrutable tables and, in later formulations, interminable towers of numbers to calculate the odds that an electron circling an atom would jump to a higher or lower orbit. The next year, Erwin Schrödinger introduced his “wave mechanics.” It used waves to track, for instance, the probability of a particle being found at a certain location in space. While the pictures evoked by these two physicists looked completely distinct, they yielded identical predictions. Heisenberg and Schrödinger had come up with two radically different incarnations of one theory. But what was that theory?

The question fascinated David Hilbert, a renowned mathematician who had devoted much of his life to rebuilding physics on a sturdy foundation of crisp axioms. He got von Neumann thinking about the problem in the mid-1920s. In 1927 the 23-year-old prodigy — building on insights from Paul Dirac — solved it in a single-author trilogy of papers.

“The ideas specifically were von Neumann’s, but the inspiration — why do you axiomatize and what for — this is something that he took from Hilbert,” said Leo Corry, a historian of mathematics.

These papers laid out the rules for quantum mechanics, carefully defining the theory’s central objects and how they behaved. Von Neumann showed that Heisenberg’s towers and Schrödinger’s waves were reflections of the same entity, just as 0.5 and ½ indicate the same point on the number line. They both represented the main character in quantum mechanics: the quantum state.

Everything has a state. A coin can read heads or tails. A grandfather clock’s bob can take on any number of positions as it swings. Most of physics amounts to capturing an object’s state and predicting how it will change.

Von Neumann’s quantum rules complicate the notion of a state. Before you observe a quantum object, it does not have a fixed set of properties, such as a specific position. Instead it has a combination of possible properties unique to quantum mechanics — a “quantum superposition.” A superposition combines, for instance, all possible places the particle might end up being. Those possibilities can be precise and informative; perhaps there is a 99% chance you’ll find your particle to your left and a 1% chance you’ll find it to your right. You know how to place your bets, but you can’t know for sure if you’ve won until you check.

Von Neumann rendered the quantum state as a mathematical arrow called a vector. This arrow points in some direction through a space capturing all the possible futures of any quantum object — a Hilbert space.

Imagine a quantum traffic light with three possible states — red, yellow, or green. Its arrow exists in a three-dimensional Hilbert space, where the three axes represent the three possible future colors. Until the moment the light is observed, it doesn’t have a color, but rather a mixture of possible colors. So its arrow points into the space’s central region. The more closely the arrow aligns with, say, the red axis, the more likely the light is to shine red.

The state of any object, from an electron to a galaxy, can be captured by such a vector, pointing in some direction through such a Hilbert space. This is von Neumann’s first rule of quantum mechanics.

What Happens in Hilbert Space?

An arrow moves through Hilbert space in one of two ways. Von Neumann’s other commandments specify how.

The first possibility corresponds to what happens before an observation. As the world influences the object, changing its state, the arrow turns smoothly through Hilbert space. It might get closer to the green axis, which would make our traffic light more likely to be measured as green, or to red or yellow. The point is that all this happens smoothly and predictably.

Then, if you actually observe the system, the vector will instantly and randomly snap onto either the red, yellow, or green axis. The more aligned it is with one axis, the more likely it is to snap to that axis instead of the others, but its fate is ultimately unpredictable. Let’s say it goes green. You’ll observe a green light, and there is now a 100% chance that it will still be green in subsequent measurements, because the arrow is fully aligned with the green axis. The quantum superposition is no more.

What Properties Define Hilbert Space?

The more possible futures an object has, the bigger its Hilbert space. A coinlike particle with two possible futures is a “qubit,” the computational building block of quantum computers. It has a two-dimensional Hilbert space. Our three-color traffic light has a three-dimensional Hilbert space. But that’s just the beginning. A freely floating particle could be found in any location in the universe, so its Hilbert space must span an infinite number of dimensions.

This size — whether it’s two dimensions or an infinite number — is the only fundamental feature of a Hilbert space, according to von Neumann’s rules. The axes are arbitrary and imagined by us; they aren’t intrinsic to the space.

Consider an electron. It has one state, one arrow, pointing in a vast Hilbert space. Its Hilbert space spans all possible measurements — energy, position, momentum, etc. If you are curious where the electron might be, you can mark the space with the axes that represent possible positions. If you are wondering where the particle might be going, you apply a different set of axes, those representing possible momenta. No matter which measurement you intend to make, the underlying Hilbert space remains the same.

This freedom to carve up Hilbert space as we see fit is what allowed Heisenberg and Schrödinger to come up with two distinct versions of the same theory. Heisenberg’s picture essentially put in axes and let them rotate around the vector, while Schrödinger’s picture did the opposite: It put in a fixed set of axes and let the vector rotate relative to them. They were two completely different mathematical perspectives on the same arrows, in the same Hilbert spaces.

In the first of his 1927 papers, von Neumann laid out two mathematical criteria that defined such a space. First, it had to be “complete.” It couldn’t be missing any regions or points. And second, you had to be able to calculate the alignment between a state and an axis, which you can visualize by imagining a light shining straight down onto an arrow so it casts a shadow on an axis. (The longer the shadow, the more aligned with that axis the arrow is.) The space had to allow for this operation, known as an inner product. Any space with these two features, no matter its size or origin, was a Hilbert space.

“This was a major step in creating what we call Hilbert space quantum mechanics,” said Miklós Rédei, a philosopher of physics at the London School of Economics. “It’s a beautiful example of how mathematical generalization or abstraction takes place.”

Von Neumann referred to these abstract spaces as Hilbert spaces because his mentor Hilbert had been the first mathematician to explore specific spaces with infinite dimensions in the early 1900s. Hilbert’s work had relied on those spaces being complete and having an inner product, but he didn’t think of them as examples of a more general class of spaces until his protégé grouped them together. The older mathematician may have been surprised to find his name attached to this new mathematical structure. “Dr. von Neumann, I am really curious to know what these Hilbert spaces are, after all,” Hilbert reportedly asked during a 1929 lecture.

Is Hilbert Space Real or Just an Abstraction?

A century after the birth of quantum mechanics, the theory has left physicists in an awkward position. We live in a world where objects change position as they move through three dimensions of physical space. But our most fundamental theory takes place somewhere else, in von Neumann’s vast realm of possibilities. What does that imply about the reality of our world, or that of Hilbert space?

Mathematically Crucial Fine Print

In quantum physics, Hilbert spaces use complex numbers, which involve the imaginary number i, and negative regions. But von Neumann’s fourth commandment guarantees that the odds of any possibility will always come out as a real, positive number.

To Sean Carroll, a philosopher and physicist at Johns Hopkins University, the message is clear. If quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory of nature, then Hilbert space should be considered the fundamental theater of reality, he argued in a 2022 paper. One of his lines of research seeks to distill our familiar world from the disorienting Hilbert space that encapsulates all the ways the universe could possibly be.

Other physicists take a more pragmatic stance. Jonathan Sorce, a physicist at Princeton University, says that Hilbert space is a handy mathematical construction that is remarkably useful for describing many quantum systems — but not all of them. He belongs to a community of researchers searching for a mathematical construction that can describe the fabric of space and time as a quantum object. Such a theory is a prerequisite for answering big questions such as what goes on at the heart of a black hole.

Physicists asking these questions have recently focused on an even more abstract space that seems especially well suited for their purposes. This kind of space is made up of the things you could do to a Hilbert space, such as slicing it up in different ways or rotating one slice into another. In this arena, they have found that black holes seem a bit less mysterious.

This sort of über-space is known today as a von Neumann algebra. Von Neumann himself helped develop it as a potential remedy for some logical inconsistencies with Hilbert space that troubled him. “I would like to make a confession which may seem immoral: I do not believe in Hilbert space anymore,” he wrote in a 1935 letter while exploring the virtues of algebras.

Sorce, for his part, doesn’t share von Neumann’s desire for one space to rule them all. He’s content to use whichever mathematical construction best suits the quantum object he’s studying. Often it’s a Hilbert space. Sometimes it’s a von Neumann algebra. And occasionally it might even be one of the many other spaces mathematicians have cooked up over the last century.

“There’s a whole zoo of these things,” he said.

The 5 Quantum Commandments of John von Neumann

1.An arrow in Hilbert space shall represent the quantum state of any object.

2.Altering the object shall make the arrow rotate smoothly through Hilbert space to represent a new state.

3.Distinct axes in Hilbert space shall reflect different possible sets of properties of the object.

4.The shadow the arrow casts onto an axis shall encode the odds of that possibility being realized when a measurement takes place.

5.Upon measurement, the arrow shall randomly and instantaneously jump to align with the axis representing the observed outcome, and the object shall acquire a fully determined property.

Often it’s a Hilbert space. Sometimes it’s a von Neumann algebra. And occasionally it might even be one of the many other spaces mathematicians have cooked up over the last century.
“There’s a whole zoo of these things,” he said.

blocks.x: The 5 Quantum Commandments of John von Neumann
1.An arrow in Hilbert space shall represent the quantum state of any object.
2.Altering the object shall make the arrow rotate smoothly through Hilbert space to represent a new state.
3.Distinct axes in Hilbert space shall reflect different possible sets of properties of the object.
4.The shadow the arrow casts onto an axis shall encode the odds of that possibility being realized when a measurement takes place.
5.Upon measurement, the arrow shall randomly and instantaneously jump to align with the axis representing the observed outcome, and the object shall acquire a fully determined property.

Netflix 首次公布院线票房，《La Bola Negra》四馆收入 27.75 万美元

iPhone Duo 溢价回落、机械臂版 HomeView 正在开发

据彭博社 Mark Gurman 报道，苹果正开发一款配备机械臂的高端智能家居屏幕，代号 J595，计划于 2027 年或 2028 年推出。该设备预计搭载约 9 英寸屏幕，可旋转 360 度，并能识别说话者、自动转向对应的人；它将定位高于现款 HomeView，具体名称尚未确定。


iPhone Duo 方面，据新京报贝壳财经，截至 10 月 17 日 19 时，得物平台黑色 512GB 版本的二级市场溢价为 3150 元，较前一晚的 6469 元回落超过五成。界面新闻采访的经销商也表示，收货溢价已有回落。


首发库存仍不明确。Mark Gurman 10 月 18 日在 X 表示，苹果门店尚未统一要求劝退无预约顾客，部分门店仍在核对到货量与预订订单。iPhone Duo 将于 10 月 23 日正式发售。


曝三星拟采用台积电 3nm 工艺，为英伟达定制 HBM

据《首尔经济日报》10 月 18 日援引产业消息人士报道，英伟达正与三星、台积电共同设计定制高带宽内存 NVHBM，计划使用台积电 3nm 工艺制造底部的逻辑芯片。该芯片负责控制内存信号，是决定数据传输速度的重要部分。


报道称，这一方案会把原本位于 GPU 上的内存控制器移到底部逻辑芯片，为 GPU 腾出更多空间放置计算电路。相较标准 HBM4E，设计目标是带宽最多提高 30%、功耗降低 15%。


合作也涉及产能：三星现有底部逻辑芯片产线难以承接全部定制需求，台积电可补充供给。三星同时在验证自家 2nm 工艺生产 NVHBM 底部逻辑芯片的方案，报道并未将后续生产锁定为台积电独家。


英伟达否认 RTX 5090 停产，称供应链仍受限制

英伟达个人计算业务高级副总裁 Jeff Fisher 于 10 月 16 日在台北出席 RTX Spark 电脑开售活动时，否认 GeForce RTX 5090 即将停产的传闻，表示这款旗舰游戏显卡仍是产品线的重要部分，英伟达将持续供货。


Fisher 同时承认，当前供应链存在限制。他说，这并非英伟达单独面临的问题，全球行业都受到供应紧张影响，团队正努力把产品推向市场。


对于英伟达近年在 AI 领域的扩张，Fisher 强调了游戏业务的基础地位：团队多年建立 GeForce 的游戏生态，由 GeForce 发展出 CUDA，再走向加速计算和 AI。他表示，公司仍对游戏市场保持承诺。


蔚来联创：蔚来第三季度终端销量首次分别超过 BBA 三家厂商


10 月 17 日，蔚来联合创始人、总裁秦力洪披露，按威尔森终端销量数据，蔚来公司第三季度在中国市场累计销售 111638 辆，季度销量首次分别超过奔驰、宝马、奥迪三家德系豪华厂商。


同一统计口径下，宝马厂商（含 MINI）为 107210 辆，奔驰厂商（含迈巴赫、smart）为 99592 辆，奥迪厂商为 94597 辆。这里比较的是蔚来公司的合计销量与三家厂商各自的销量。


从地域来看，蔚来公司在 8 个省级行政区、40 个城市的第三季度销量超过 BBA 三家厂商；在 12 个省级行政区、94 个城市，至少超过其中一家。上述城市既包括北上广深、成都、武汉，也包括汕头、宜昌、鹤岗等。


Anthropic 为芯片融资拟向黑石提供逾 10% 收益率


据路透社援引英国《金融时报》报道，Anthropic 正就最新一笔芯片交易安排融资，并拟向黑石提供超过 10% 的收益率。相关安排仍是拟议交易。


《金融时报》援引知情人士称，黑石旗下基金计划为这笔交易投入 90 亿美元。这笔资金将用于投资与芯片相关的债务，该债务以 Anthropic 未来五年为使用这些芯片而支付的租赁款项作为支持。


智界拟取得独立造车资质，内部人士确认独立上市计划


10 月 17 日，智界汽车内部人士向第一财经确认，公司在相关公示结束并获批后，将取得独立造车资质；该人士同时确认，智界未来计划独立上市。


工信部 10 月 16 日公示的第 412 批《道路机动车辆生产企业及产品公告》，已将安徽智界新能源汽车有限公司列入「拟发布新准入车辆生产企业」清单，公示期至 10 月 23 日。


公示中的智界生产地址，正是奇瑞同期申请注销的芜湖厂区。智界内部人士将此概括为「奇瑞的工厂给到了智界」。这一步涉及现有工厂生产主体的转移，目前仍处于公示待批阶段。


智界此前已在奇瑞内部独立核算、自主经营。今年 6 月底的工商变更后，奇瑞持股由 100% 降至 85%，两家股权投资合伙企业各持 7.5%。


Tibo 回应 Codex 用户许愿：五项建议中有两项正在做

10 月 17 日，OpenAI 的 Codex 与 ChatGPT 团队成员 Tibo Sottiaux 在 X 上回应一份用户许愿清单，称团队「正在做其中两项」。


这份清单由用户 AI Fun 提出，具体希望：

取消 Plus 的 5 小时用量限制；


向 Plus 用户开放 dot；


将 ultrafast 的加速幅度提高到 15 倍；


将 Pro 20x 的用量翻倍；


将 GPT-6.1 Sol 的输出速度提高到至少每秒 50 个 token。

在近期更新中，他还介绍了 Codex 与 Work 提高实际可用额度的做法：在子智能体之间复用上下文、延长上下文缓存时间，并通过优化请求路由提高缓存命中率。


另一项已公布的变化是 ChatGPT Space 增加幻灯片支持，先面向 Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 用户开放。


长安董事长：国内车市承压，要全力聚焦海外

长安汽车新任董事长赵非在 10 月 16 日的媒体沟通会上谈到，国内汽车市场下滑严重，海外仍有机会，长安要全力聚焦海外发展。他对国内竞争的判断是：


国内的这种竞争态势，有时候其实已经进入到一个马太效应、洗牌的这么一个阶段。


他认为，部分友商的非理性行为会影响产品定价和市场的可持续发展。


据第一财经和界面新闻的现场报道，赵非认为，长安在新能源和智能化方面相对部分海外车企具备优势。但过去「国内卖得好，再卖到全球」的做法已经行不通，欧洲用户与国内用户的需求不同，北欧和南欧也有差异。


针对这些差异，他提出，产品定义应以全球用户需求为起点，制定全球大单品策略。按照长安的规划，2027 年全球销量目标为 300 万辆以上，其中海外目标为 150 万辆。他同时强调「量利并重」，不参与价格战。


对于欧洲市场，赵非表示，当地合作伙伴预计很快公布，明年上半年将有产品落地。进入欧洲需要坚持长期化、本地化和体系化，不能「赚一把就跑」。海外、产品、效率和品牌整合将是长安接下来的四个聚焦方向，其中海外排在首位。


DeepSeek 更新模型，能按需求生成游戏和 3D 场景

10 月 17 日，DeepSeek 将 V4.1 Flash 升级至 Flash-1017，网页端、App 和 API 已同步更新，模型调用方式与价格不变。


新版增强了从零开发游戏、搭建 3D 场景的能力。官方用 DeepSeek Harness 演示了故宫 3D 建模、网页版赛车，以及基于 Godot 的《传送门 2》复刻。模型权重采用 MIT 许可开源，Harness 也已适配。


DeepSeek 同日开放搜索与网页抓取 API，分别用于搜索网页、提取网页正文，两项接口均按成功请求计费，每 1000 次 5 元。通过 Harness、Claude Code 或 Codex 使用 DeepSeek API 时，服务端工具调用产生的搜索与抓取目前免费，11 月 1 日 00:00 起收费。


相关阅读：刚刚，DeepSeek 发布新模型！用「许愿式编程」刷新斩杀线


Meta 删除争议抓取条款，称未扩大 AI 训练权限


Meta 再次修改商业条款，删除了一段引发新闻网站担忧的内容。此前的条文称，Meta 可使用商业账户关联域名、网页或 URL 的内容，来提供、开发、改进和训练旗下产品与服务。


据 The Verge 报道，康奈尔大学数字与信息法教授 James Grimmelmann 等法律人士认为，这种表述可能让 Meta 获得免费抓取新闻网站、训练 AI 的权限，甚至覆盖网站通过 robots.txt 表达的限制。


Meta 发言人 Daniel Roberts 则表示，被整合的抓取条款仅适用于广告和商业产品，公司已在条文中澄清这一点。他强调，Meta 使用网络爬虫的方式没有改变，内容所有者仍可通过 robots.txt 表达偏好，此次更新也没有赋予 Meta 凌驾于这些偏好之上的新权利。


TikTok 暂停纪录片《马斯克》广告账户，发行方正在申诉

据《好莱坞报道》独家报道，TikTok 暂停了纪录片《Musk》的广告账户，理由是多次发布违反平台政策的政治内容。发行商 Bleecker Street 确认收到「永久暂停」通知，目前正在申诉。


这项限制针对付费广告和内容加热，影片的普通 TikTok 账号仍保持活跃。《好莱坞报道》查看的邮件显示，预告片等素材在拒登与申诉之间反复流转；TikTok 方面还曾以静态图片为由拦下一则引用影评的广告。


《Musk》由 Alex Gibney 执导，调查历时三年多，涉及马斯克的企业、收购 Twitter 及政治活动。影片正在北美扩映至 470 多块银幕，发行商对广告限制发生在扩映周末表示失望。TikTok 未就该报道发表评论。


Zeabur 宣布逐步停运，12 月 31 日前关闭全部服务器

云部署平台 Zeabur 创始人林沅霖在用户邮件中宣布，平台将逐步结束运营，部分服务从 12 月 1 日起陆续停止，所有专用服务器与共享集群将在 12 月 31 日前关闭。


具体安排分为两类：专用服务器从 12 月 1 日起停用续费，并按各自到期日在当月陆续关机；共享集群同日起暂停运行中的服务，用户仍可手动恢复，以便备份。平台已停止新的专用服务器与域名购买，并开始受理账户余额退款，域名也可自助转出。


这封邮件发布前，Zeabur 在 8 月底和 10 月接连发生安全事件。官方状态页确认，第二次事件涉及平台数据库被读取，暴露内容包括服务环境变量、账户信息及 API Token，部分 Google Cloud 专用服务器也遭到未授权访问。林沅霖表示，再次遭到攻击后，团队重新评估了持续运营所需投入和能够承担的责任，最终决定停运。


团队将提供迁移指南，以及可供 Claude Code、Codex 使用的 Markdown 指南和 Skills。12 月 31 日是全部服务停止的日期，各项服务仍须按自身到期日提前备份和迁移。


Anthropic 拟拨出 5% 股份设公益基金，仍需股东批准


Anthropic 宣布，拟将公司 5% 的股份划入新设的 Anthropic Public Benefit Fund，方案仍需股东批准。此后，公司价值每较设定基准增长 50%，董事会可酌情再增加 2% 的股份，并非自动划拨。


基金将以公司全资持有的有限责任公司形式设立，可用于向非营利组织捐赠、向特定群体直接分配资金，以及应对 AI 对就业市场的冲击。Anthropic 称，此前已承诺投入 2 亿美元研究和应对就业影响，新基金可支持更大范围的行动。基金持有的公司股权不会用于美国或海外的游说和政治捐赠。


连同创始人和员工此前的捐赠承诺，约 20% 的 Anthropic 股份将被用于公共利益；未来估值达到特定门槛时，比例还可能增加。公司计划在未来数月公布基金治理、结构及估值门槛细节。


迪士尼拟接收 Character.AI 逾 60 名员工，三年薪酬约 1.8 亿美元


据彭博社援引破产法庭文件报道，迪士尼同意聘用 Character.AI 的 60 多名员工，覆盖该公司大部分团队，前三年的合计薪酬约为 1.8 亿美元。迪士尼还将另拨 3000 万美元用于后续留任奖励，其中部分款项会在交易完成一周年、两周年时支付。


这笔团队安排与资产收购价分开计算。迪士尼此前提出以 2000 万美元购买 Character.AI 部分资产，并在后者申请破产前已支付其中一部分。Character.AI 前 CEO Karandeep Anand 则已先行加入迪士尼，出任这家娱乐公司的首位 CTO。


Character.AI 于 10 月 12 日申请破产保护，面临较高运营成本、与未成年人安全有关的诉讼和政府调查。迪士尼的安排仍需破产法官批准；若出现更高报价，11 月可能举行破产拍卖，员工也可与其他公司面谈。


相关阅读：AI 陪伴鼻祖破产，你能导出聊天记录，却带不走 TA


孟樸：AI 将走向端云协同，智能体会主动调用应用和设备

据新浪科技报道，高通中国区董事长孟樸在东北亚（沈阳）人才交流大会暨人工智能赋能产业发展大会上表示，AI 将越来越多地走向云端与边缘协同，大量任务正扩展到手机、PC、汽车、机器人和工业设备，终端侧 AI 正发挥更重要的作用。


他给出的分工是：云端拥有强大的模型与算力，适合处理复杂、资源密集型任务；终端在实时响应、可靠性和个性化体验方面有自身优势。


智能体会进一步加速这一趋势：AI 理解人的意图和所处场景后，可以主动调用不同的应用、服务和设备，共同完成任务，计算体验因而逐步从以应用为中心转向以智能体为中心。


在产业落地上，孟樸强调，应把终端、汽车、制造业、开发者、高校和科研机构连接起来，让人才、技术与产业协同。

特斯拉高管详解 Roadster「飞行」原理：风扇吸地、氮气推进器助推

特斯拉 Roadster 的「飞行」功能如何实现？MotorTrend 记者在 10 月 16 日发布的现场报道中，记录了特斯拉车辆工程负责人 Lars Moravy 对原型车的技术讲解：车底风扇负责增加抓地力，另有压缩氮气推进器提供额外推力。

风扇吸地：车尾四台风扇抽走底盘下方空气，配合下降的侧裙形成低压区，即使静止也能产生下压力。主动空气动力部件还包括前翼、前舱盖和大型尾翼，部分执行器采用 Optimus 机器人的踝关节技术。


氮气助推：Thrust 版用 200 升高压储罐向四个冷气推进器供气；单座 Rocket 版再以副驾驶空间容纳额外 400 升储罐，总容量增至 600 升、推进器增至十个，分别用于车身抬升、转向和向前加速。它们通过释放压缩气体产生推力，无需燃烧。


动力与进度：后轮分别由两台电机驱动，总功率为 1 兆瓦，电池采用 4680 电芯。记者看到的仍是具备量产意图的原型车，特斯拉给出的量产目标为 2028 年，实际性能与交付安排仍待后续确认。

RTX Spark 笔记本正式开售，2599 美元起

英伟达 10 月 16 日宣布，搭载 RTX Spark 的笔记本电脑正式开售，全球产品起价为 2599 美元，具体配置与价格因地区而异。


首批阵容覆盖华硕 ProArt P14／P16、戴尔 XPS 16、惠普 OmniBook Ultra／OmniBook X 14、联想 Yoga Pro 9n、微软 Surface Laptop Ultra，以及微星 Prestige N16 系列。


RTX Spark 将 Grace CPU 与 Blackwell RTX GPU 集成在同一颗超级芯片中，最高配备 128GB 统一内存，官方标称最高提供 1 PFLOPS 的 FP4 AI 算力。共享内存可用于本地模型、AI 智能体和大型 3D 场景，联发科参与了定制 CPU 的设计。


软件适配也随整机到来：Photoshop 和 Premiere 的原生支持先以测试版提供；Windows on Arm 获得 PyTorch-CUDA 构建，英伟达称已支持最热门 1.5 万个 Python 包中的 97%。首发游戏阵容包括《赛博朋克 2077》《堡垒之夜》《漫威争锋》和《NBA 2K27》，兼容游戏可使用 DLSS、光线追踪及 Reflex 等技术。

吉利星瑞 L PLUS 上市，限时 10.97 万元起

新车长宽高为 4956×1915×1505mm，轴距 2845mm。混动版本搭载 i-HEV 系统，1.5TD 发动机最大功率 120kW，驱动电机最大功率 175kW，官方公布的 WLTC 百公里油耗为 3.98 升；2.0TD 燃油版搭配 8AT 变速箱。


两条动力线的顶配均提供千里浩瀚 H5 辅助驾驶方案，传感器包含 1 颗激光雷达、3 颗毫米波雷达和 11 颗高清摄像头，支持城市及高速领航辅助驾驶、记忆泊车等功能。


座舱配备 Flyme Auto 2、15.4 英寸 2.5K 中控屏和 10.2 英寸仪表，不同版本提供 CCD 可变阻尼悬架、座椅通风加热与按摩等配置。


埃安 Ray7 开启预售，12.88 万元起

10 月 17 日，埃安 Ray 系列首款中大型纯电轿车 Ray7 开启预售，共推出 5 款配置，预售价为 12.88 万元至 15.88 万元。


Ray7 采用后驱布局，车长 4960mm、轴距 2920mm，提供 530 公里和 702 公里两档 CLTC 续航。新车搭载华为 DriveONE 多合一电驱，顶配车型还配备 EMB 全电线控制动系统及 iTrack 智能扭矩控制系统。


驾驶辅助方面，激光版配备 192 线激光雷达，采用文远知行一段式端到端大模型。座舱搭载骁龙 8295P 芯片，配备 24GB 内存、128GB 存储及 15.6 英寸 2.5K 中控屏。


底盘采用前双叉臂、后五连杆悬架，并配备 FSD 自适应阻尼减振器。新车换用埃安全新品牌标识与「量子星环」灯组，提供 7 种车身颜色。


AMG 首款独立研发纯电 SUV 发布，GT 63 零百加速 2.7 秒

梅赛德斯-AMG 发布 GT SUV，这是品牌首款从零开始独立研发的全尺寸 SUV，也是 AMG.EA 纯电架构的第二款车型。新车提供 GT 53、GT 55 和 GT 63 三个版本，GT 53 德国含税建议零售价 113050 欧元起，10 月 20 日开放订购；另外两款计划于 2027 年春季推出。

高配车型提供 128kWh 电池，官方公布的 WLTP 续航最高 700 公里，直流快充功率最高 710kW。按厂商初步测试条件，充电 10 分钟可增加约 450 公里 WLTP 续航。车辆还配有后轮转向、主动液压侧倾控制，并通过真实发动机录音、模拟换挡及座椅振动呈现 AMG 声浪体验。


Reason Network 更新独立运行模式，让不同电脑上的 AI 编程助手直接通信

Reason 更新了开源项目 Reason Network，10 月 17 日发布的 0.10.4 版加入无需 Reason 账户的独立使用方式，并支持原 tincan 用户迁移。它把团队成员不同电脑上的 AI 编程助手连在一起，让一个会话可以直接询问另一个会话，无须人工反复转述。


每台电脑运行一个轻量后台程序，团队通讯录会显示谁的 Agent 在线、正在处理哪个仓库和分支、处于忙碌还是空闲状态，以及当前任务。支持范围包括 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、Copilot CLI 和 OpenCode；其中 Claude Code、Codex 可以在现有会话里接收消息。


电脑之间优先点对点通信，同一局域网或跨互联网均可连接；直连失败时，经只能看到加密数据的中继传递消息。项目采用 MIT 或 Apache 2.0 许可证。


自动检测多名 Agent 同时修改同一文件的功能仍在后续开发清单中。现阶段提供的是工作状态共享和会话通信，不能自动阻止代码覆盖。


VAST 开源 EdenLive，称单张 RTX 5090 可实时生成 720P 画面

VAST 发布并开放实时生成式渲染模型 EdenLive 的代码与 5B、14B 模型权重。团队公布，5B 模型在单张 RTX 5090 上可生成 720P 画面，速度超过 24FPS，并支持分钟级连续生成。


EdenLive 接收简化场景或参考视频、目标首帧和文字提示：参考画面确定布局、镜头与运动，首帧与提示词控制外观和画风。游戏规则、角色位置和交互状态由上游程序或引擎维护，模型负责把参考画面渲染成更精细的视觉内容。官方展示了游戏漫游、视频换风格和具身操作视频增强等用法。


配套的 Game Prototype Turbo 可从提示词生成可玩原型，再接入渲染链路。授权按组件区分：主要视频模型采用 Apache 2.0，视觉编码器沿用 DINOv3 授权；工作台用于生成写实首帧的 FLUX 组件限非商业、非生产用途，视频生成管线本身不依赖该组件。


苹果据称筹备机械臂版 HomeView，可转向说话者


苹果正在规划配备电动机械臂的高端 HomeView。据 9to5Mac 引述 Mark Gurman 的 Power On 报道，这款代号 J595 的设备目标是在 2027 年或 2028 年推出。


报道描述，它的屏幕约为 9 英寸，大于当前 HomeView 的 7 英寸；机械臂可让显示屏旋转 360 度。设备计划利用语音识别判断谁在说话，再自动将屏幕转向那个人，供围坐在不同位置的人使用。


这一版本定位高于现有 HomeView，而非替代当前机型。机械臂、识别说话者与自动转向均属于研发计划，相关功能和上市窗口尚未由苹果正式公布。

Swisse 两批次产品铅超标被召回，品牌称未进入中国市场


海关总署进出口食品安全局 10 月 17 日发布风险警示，澳大利亚药品管理局通报，两批次 Swisse「Beauty Skin Regeneration+」产品被检出铅含量超出标准限值，企业将召回相关产品。


通告列出的产品编号为 01-141-20602，批号分别为 144520、143217，有效期至 2028 年 7 月。目前，国内暂未发现涉事产品通过一般贸易渠道进口。海关提醒消费者核对通过跨境电商、携带、代购等渠道可能持有的产品，立即停止使用涉事批次，并关注澳方后续信息。


据南方都市报报道，Swisse 于 10 月 18 日回应称，澳洲公司在例行自检中发现问题，已主动召回相关批次。品牌方表示，涉事批次仅存在于澳洲，已在当地可控环节召回，未流入消费者端，也从未进入中国市场。


海关的风险警示针对具体产品与批次，品牌方上述回应则涉及其对流向和召回情况的核查。消费者核对时需对应产品编号、批号及有效期。

iPhone Duo 溢价回落、机械臂版 HomeView 正在开发
据彭博社 Mark Gurman 报道，苹果正开发一款配备机械臂的高端智能家居屏幕，代号 J595，计划于 2027 年或 2028 年推出。该设备预计搭载约 9 英寸屏幕，可旋转 360 度，并能识别说话者、自动转向对应的人；它将定位高于现款 HomeView，具体名称尚未确定。
iPhone Duo 方面，据新京报贝壳财经，截至 10 月 17 日 19 时，得物平台黑色 512GB 版本的二级市场溢价为 3150 元，较前一晚的 6469 元回落超过五成。界面新闻采访的经销商也表示，收货溢价已有回落。
首发库存仍不明确。Mark Gurman 10 月 18 日在 X 表示，苹果门店尚未统一要求劝退无预约顾客，部分门店仍在核对到货量与预订订单。iPhone Duo 将于 10 月 23 日正式发售。
曝三星拟采用台积电 3nm 工艺，为英伟达定制 HBM
据《首尔经济日报》10 月 18 日援引产业消息人士报道，英伟达正与三星、台积电共同设计定制高带宽内存 NVHBM，计划使用台积电 3nm 工艺制造底部的逻辑芯片。该芯片负责控制内存信号，是决定数据传输速度的重要部分。
报道称，这一方案会把原本位于 GPU 上的内存控制器移到底部逻辑芯片，为 GPU 腾出更多空间放置计算电路。相较标准 HBM4E，设计目标是带宽最多提高 30%、功耗降低 15%。
合作也涉及产能：三星现有底部逻辑芯片产线难以承接全部定制需求，台积电可补充供给。三星同时在验证自家 2nm 工艺生产 NVHBM 底部逻辑芯片的方案，报道并未将后续生产锁定为台积电独家。
英伟达否认 RTX 5090 停产，称供应链仍受限制
英伟达个人计算业务高级副总裁 Jeff Fisher 于 10 月 16 日在台北出席 RTX Spark 电脑开售活动时，否认 GeForce RTX 5090 即将停产的传闻，表示这款旗舰游戏显卡仍是产品线的重要部分，英伟达将持续供货。
Fisher 同时承认，当前供应链存在限制。他说，这并非英伟达单独面临的问题，全球行业都受到供应紧张影响，团队正努力把产品推向市场。

Reason 更新了开源项目 Reason Network，10 月 17 日发布的 0.10.4 版加入无需 Reason 账户的独立使用方式，并支持原 tincan 用户迁移。它把团队成员不同电脑上的 AI 编程助手连在一起，让一个会话可以直接询问另一个会话，无须人工反复转述。
每台电脑运行一个轻量后台程序，团队通讯录会显示谁的 Agent 在线、正在处理哪个仓库和分支、处于忙碌还是空闲状态，以及当前任务。支持范围包括 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Gemini CLI、Copilot CLI 和 OpenCode；其中 Claude Code、Codex 可以在现有会话里接收消息。
电脑之间优先点对点通信，同一局域网或跨互联网均可连接；直连失败时，经只能看到加密数据的中继传递消息。项目采用 MIT 或 Apache 2.0 许可证。
自动检测多名 Agent 同时修改同一文件的功能仍在后续开发清单中。现阶段提供的是工作状态共享和会话通信，不能自动阻止代码覆盖。
VAST 开源 EdenLive，称单张 RTX 5090 可实时生成 720P 画面
VAST 发布并开放实时生成式渲染模型 EdenLive 的代码与 5B、14B 模型权重。团队公布，5B 模型在单张 RTX 5090 上可生成 720P 画面，速度超过 24FPS，并支持分钟级连续生成。
EdenLive 接收简化场景或参考视频、目标首帧和文字提示：参考画面确定布局、镜头与运动，首帧与提示词控制外观和画风。游戏规则、角色位置和交互状态由上游程序或引擎维护，模型负责把参考画面渲染成更精细的视觉内容。官方展示了游戏漫游、视频换风格和具身操作视频增强等用法。
配套的 Game Prototype Turbo 可从提示词生成可玩原型，再接入渲染链路。授权按组件区分：主要视频模型采用 Apache 2.0，视觉编码器沿用 DINOv3 授权；工作台用于生成写实首帧的 FLUX 组件限非商业、非生产用途，视频生成管线本身不依赖该组件。
苹果据称筹备机械臂版 HomeView，可转向说话者
苹果正在规划配备电动机械臂的高端 HomeView。据 9to5Mac 引述 Mark Gurman 的 Power On 报道，这款代号 J595 的设备目标是在 2027 年或 2028 年推出。
报道描述，它的屏幕约为 9 英寸，大于当前 HomeView 的 7 英寸；机械臂可让显示屏旋转 360 度。设备计划利用语音识别判断谁在说话，再自动将屏幕转向那个人，供围坐在不同位置的人使用。
这一版本定位高于现有 HomeView，而非替代当前机型。机械臂、识别说话者与自动转向均属于研发计划，相关功能和上市窗口尚未由苹果正式公布。
Swisse 两批次产品铅超标被召回，品牌称未进入中国市场
海关总署进出口食品安全局 10 月 17 日发布风险警示，澳大利亚药品管理局通报，两批次 Swisse「Beauty Skin Regeneration+」产品被检出铅含量超出标准限值，企业将召回相关产品。
通告列出的产品编号为 01-141-20602，批号分别为 144520、143217，有效期至 2028 年 7 月。目前，国内暂未发现涉事产品通过一般贸易渠道进口。海关提醒消费者核对通过跨境电商、携带、代购等渠道可能持有的产品，立即停止使用涉事批次，并关注澳方后续信息。
据南方都市报报道，Swisse 于 10 月 18 日回应称，澳洲公司在例行自检中发现问题，已主动召回相关批次。品牌方表示，涉事批次仅存在于澳洲，已在当地可控环节召回，未流入消费者端，也从未进入中国市场。
海关的风险警示针对具体产品与批次，品牌方上述回应则涉及其对流向和召回情况的核查。消费者核对时需对应产品编号、批号及有效期。
刘德华、杨子姗主演《白衣逆行者》定档 11 月 6 日
电影《白衣逆行者》宣布于 11 月 6 日上映，并发布「76 个日夜」版定档预告。影片由邱礼涛执导，刘德华、杨子姗领衔主演，秦海璐、余皑磊、韩童生等参演。
故事回到 2020 年初，大学教授沈君（刘德华饰）与医生袁楚楚（杨子姗饰）夫妇赶赴武汉，与护士长田璐（秦海璐饰）、医生钟凌云（余皑磊饰）等当地医护人员共同救治病患，通过不同职业的普通人展现这段时期的守望相助。
《Imperium》获伦敦电影节最佳影片
第 70 届 BFI 伦敦电影节于当地时间 10 月 18 日公布竞赛单元奖项。谢尔盖·洛兹尼察执导的《Imperium》获得最佳影片，这部作品利用意大利摄影师拍摄的档案影像，重访 20 世纪 70 年代初的苏联。
泰国导演 Sompot Chidgasornpongse 的首部长篇剧情片《9 Temples to Heaven》获得萨瑟兰最佳处女作奖。故事围绕一场一日朝圣展开：主人公听到母亲可能即将去世的预言后，试图通过走访九座寺庙化解危机。阿彼察邦·韦拉斯哈古参与制片。
Asmahan Bkerat 执导的《Concrete Land》获得格里尔森最佳纪录片奖，镜头聚焦约旦一个家庭面对迁离与敌意时的生活。观众奖投票将于 10 月 21 日结束，结果另行公布。
Netflix 首次公布院线票房，《La Bola Negra》四馆收入 27.75 万美元
据 Variety 报道，Netflix 首次对外公布旗下电影的院线票房。由西班牙导演 Javier Calvo 与 Javier Ambrossi 执导的《La Bola Negra》在四家影院收获 27.75 万美元，平均每家约 6.94 万美元，创下西班牙语电影开画馆均票房纪录。
影片围绕三名男性跨越世代、彼此关联的故事展开，曾获戛纳最佳导演奖及多伦多电影节观众选择奖。Netflix 计划让它在影院放映 45 天，再于 12 月 2 日上线平台。这也是该公司迄今最长的院线发行窗口。
Netflix 过去曾让《利刃出鞘 2》等电影短暂进入影院，但没有公布票房。Variety 称，公司今后也计划披露大卫·芬奇执导的《The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth》，以及 2027 年的《Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew》等作品的院线成绩。

items.text:
Sinclair ZX Spectrum Next Laptop Version 2

This project is unrelated to the official Spectrum Next Kickstarter or the Spectrum Next team. I wanted a Spectrum Next laptop. So I made one!

Having created a laptop style case for my ZX Spectrum Next dev board previously, I wanted to revisit the idea of a Spectrum laptop and address some of the issues faced in the previous version.

Some of the issues with the original laptop design were:

The hinges did not lock into position when fully closed; a lever would have been required to hold the lid shut when fully closed.

Although at the time of the build the screen worked perfectly under HDMI, the Spectrum Next firmware underwent many changes over the following months to ensure compatibility with HDMI TV's, and this unfortunately broke the compatibility with the screen chosen for the laptop.

It used an off-the-shelf USB PC keyboard. This is unacceptable in a Sinclair Spectrum laptop!

With these issues in mind, I decided to start afresh, choosing hinges from a more recent scrap laptop I had lying around and a larger HD screen that would not only support HDMI but also VGA. On top of the improved screen compatibility, I wanted to be able to use one of the fantastic keyboards from a Spectrum Next in the laptop.

With all these changes in mind, the new laptop was designed from scratch, using only a few parts of the previous design (Joystick, USB, and power jack cut-outs). The new laptop must have the following:

Original Spectrum Next keyboard

The same PCB is used in the handheld SpeccyX (to save on costs, as I have spare ones lying around)

Touchpad for games or apps that support the PS/2 mouse connector

Dual Micro-SD sockets

Stereo speakers with volume control and headphone jack

Dual joystick ports

PI USB ports

The Screen

I wanted to re-use the screen from an old, non-working laptop. The screen itself is a 14" WXGA LED screen, and when tested with a Spectrum Next, it gave a great display over HDMI and also VGA at 50 Hz.

In addition to the screen, I needed a VGA/HDMI/LCD controller board; there are plenty of these available from the likes of eBay, etc. The size of these boards isn't great for this particular project, but by removing the large unused sockets (DVI, headphones, etc.), I can at least reduce the height requirement inside the laptop.

The Keyboard

What is a better keyboard for the laptop than a genuine Spectrum Next keyboard? While it's not as thin as most modern laptop keyboards, it is sufficiently thin for this build, and I prefer the Next keyboard to most laptop keyboards. The keyboard will be "on loan" from my 2nd Spectrum Next, and I'm hoping to pick up a spare keyboard in the future, specifically for the laptop, in order to return this keyboard back to the Spectrum Next that it came from.

The PCB

Having some spare mini-boards from the handheld project I opted to use one of these for the build. It's small size lends itself well to a laptop and leaves me plenty of room inside the case for wiring and other things.

The previous version of the laptop was built around the Spectrum Next dev board, which, given its size, is not best suited to a laptop design. On top of this, they are hard to find and quite expensive.

The mini PCB, like the Spectrum Next PCB, has the ability to interface with the Raspberry PI and WiFi module, so these are also included in the laptop along with a USB splitter board for future USB devices when they become available in the firmware in the future.

Laptop Design

With the screen size already determined and I want to use the Spectrum Next keyboard, the design was built around these in the form of a standard-looking laptop. It is not as slimline as modern laptops, but that's mostly to do with me needing to use off-the-shelf components (LCD driver board, keyboard, etc.) and trying to fit them in.

3D Printing

Due to the size of the parts, initial prints were completed on my CR-10S Pro; these were made to ensure the positioning of the ports and hinges were correct. Once verified, the STL files were sent off to Shapeways to be professionally printed. Once received, I sanded down the parts and painted them black.

Completed

After lots of sanding and painting, it is time to assemble the final laptop:

A quick play of some games and demos

YouTube Video

Still to do...

Some things still need to be completed on the laptop:

Battery! Yes, I need to sort out a suitable battery and charging module.

LCD Backlight. This is always at 100% brightness; the LCD board doesn't have a way to control this. However, these screens have a pin that will allow a PWM signal to control the brightness, so I should be able to control this with the PI or something like an Arduino.

Update 19/12/2020

Some additions to the laptop will give it some of the things you would expect from a laptop. Until now, the laptop has needed to be plugged in to use; however, today I added a 12V UPS and a 10,000 mAh battery, which gives me about 6 hours of ZX Spectrum playtime while away from a plug socket.

LCD Backlight

When originally built, the LCD backlight could not be modified and was always on at 100%. What I wanted to do was make it controllable via the laptop keyboard. To do this, I picked up an Arduino Nano.

I've used these several years ago when building an LCD touchscreen Sinclair C5. With the Arduino, I can control the LCD backlight by configuring one of the output pins to send a PWM signal to the screen. By routing some of the keyboard membrane lines to the Arduino input pins, I can look for certain keyboard presses, namely the Symbol Shift and the Left/Right Cursor keys.

Holding Symbol Shift + Left I can reduce the backlight brightness; Symbol Shift + Right will increase it. This could be done using the Raspberry Pi; however, this would mean modifying the default PI software, which I do not want to do. I want to use the standard Next distribution with the laptop and have the Arduino handle laptop-specific functionality.

I did try to make a quick video showing this, but the camera auto-adjusting the brightness to compensate made it hard to show.

155 款应用拒绝豆包助手 AI 自动化操作


10 月 14 日，豆包手机助手《屏幕自动化操作声明协议》（SAEP）30 天公示期结束，官方公布名单显示，已有 155 款第三方应用拒绝 AI 自动化操作，腾讯、阿里、美团、快手旗下多款产品，连同 Kimi、DeepSeek 等 AI 产品均在名单内，堪称互联网头部厂商的集体表态。


SAEP 协议核心是将 AI 屏幕自动操作的选择权交还应用开发者，开发者可自主决定是否允许豆包助手执行屏幕识别、模拟点击等操作。公示期内应用默认不开放权限；公示结束后，未明确拒绝的应用将按风险分级逐步开放，拒绝方后续也可随时调整声明。该自动化权限仅影响 AI 代操作，不影响用户手动使用 App。


此前，努比亚 NaviX Ultra 搭载豆包手机助手发售，就出现过设备触发游戏风控等冲突，这类矛盾过去长期处于隐性博弈状态。本次拒绝名单基本集中在拥有独立流量闭环的平台，安全风险、流量主权是核心考量。SAEP 把隐性冲突转为公开规则协商，标志移动端 AI 入口权博弈正式开启。行业认为，这只是智能体时代生态确权的起点，后续权限细化、责任划分、利益分配仍需多方持续磨合。（来源：极客公园）

腾讯上线绿泡泡短剧


近日，腾讯低调上线绿泡泡短剧，主打「免费好剧，一点就看」。

绿泡泡的界面分为「免费剧场」「刷一刷」和「我的」三部分。「免费剧场」下设「AI 剧」「真人剧」「每日上新」「动漫剧」「本周必看」「百万播放」等栏目。点开中间入口「刷一刷」，上下滑动即进入沉浸式推荐流。剧集全部免费，但会在剧集之间插入广告。


《短剧小程序用户协议》显示，服务签订主体为深圳市腾讯计算机系统有限公司。协议同时写明，短剧均来自第三方提供方，包括第三方小程序、短剧制作方、授权发行方等，由其授权本服务展示、播放。


和红果短剧相比，绿泡泡的社交印记更重。除了常规排行榜，首页还有「朋友在看」的短剧推荐，以及标注「北京的朋友都在看」的地区热门榜。腾讯方面表示，为提供个性化内容，会收集用户的浏览、观看、分享、点赞、评论、收藏等记录，以及朋友看过的剧目。经过程序分析后，平台会预测用户的偏好，朋友在看什么，直接影响给相关用户推什么。


这并非腾讯首次下场做短剧。2021 年 12 月，腾讯视频发布业内首个微短剧品牌「十分剧场」，当时它只是长视频 App 里的一个频道页。2025 年 1 月，「火星短剧社」在微信上线，后改名「火星观剧」，是腾讯首款独立短剧产品。2025 年 6 月，微信上线名为「短剧」的官方小程序。到 2026 年 10 月，这个小程序已找不到入口，位置让给了绿泡泡。（来源：北京日报）

小鹏发布智能汽车解决方案业务


2026 巴黎国际车展期间，小鹏集团董事长兼 CEO 何小鹏作为巴黎汽车峰会唯一受邀的中国车企 CEO，发表重要演讲。何小鹏向与会的行业高管、全球媒体等，正式介绍其智能汽车解决方案业务：「XPENG AI ENGINEERING」，小鹏将面向全球合作伙伴开放智能汽车技术合作，输出覆盖整车研发、生产到售后的一站式能力。并将开放涵盖机器人、Robotaxi、飞行汽车、图灵 AI 芯片、物理世界基座模型等物理 AI 生态全领域的技术合作方案。


何小鹏表示：「开放已经成为小鹏与全球伙伴深化合作的关键词。我们不仅与合作伙伴共享技术，更与合作伙伴共同成长，全力支持合作伙伴掌握技术、开展自主创新。我们也欢迎全球合作伙伴加入，让我们互通技术、互学共进、携手前行」。（来源：新浪科技）

比亚迪欧洲建厂计划披露：法国候选


日前，比亚迪执行副总裁李柯在 2026 巴黎车展上表示，比亚迪将在欧洲大规模投资制造，比亚迪匈牙利工厂计划在今年第四季度启动大规模生产。


同时，比亚迪也将在欧洲建立第二、第三工厂。目前，法国已进入比亚迪欧洲建厂的候选名单。（来源：第一财经）

消息称 Anthropic 第三季度营收达 168 亿美元，已实现调整后盈利


10 月 15 日消息，据彭博社报道，知情人士透露，人工智能模型企业 Anthropic PBC 向潜在投资者表示，公司第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元，这家企业正继续推进上市计划。


知情人士称，开发 Claude 的 Anthropic 于当地时间周三在旧金山总部举办了推介会，向投资者说明，公司在该季度实现了调整后盈利。


知情人士表示，截至第三季度，Anthropic 已经实现正向自由现金流，调整后毛利率为 85%，调整后营业利润率超过 11%。


Anthropic 预计最早在 11 月 9 日那一周正式启动首次公开募股的路演工作，有望在感恩节前挂牌交易，预计年内完成上市。


知情人士表示，相关讨论仍在进行，时间安排仍有可能变动。（来源：IT 之家）

千问办公发布电商版，开启邀测


10 月 14 日，千问办公发布千问办公电商版，基于电商行业商家的日常工作场景进行了 AI 能力的重新设计和增强，尤其是针对跨多平台的电商经营场景，用一个 AI 入口驱动不同的电商平台，帮助商家完成 AI 时代的运营升级。


千问办公电商版已开启邀测，在千问办公中切换至「电商经营」模式即可体验。（来源：新浪科技）


国行 Apple Watch 上线睡眠呼吸暂停迹象提示功能


10 月 14 日消息，今日，苹果宣布在中国大陆推出 Apple Watch「睡眠呼吸暂停通知」功能，Apple 已获得移动睡眠呼吸暂停迹象提示软件由国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）批准的医疗器械注册证。


移动睡眠呼吸暂停迹象提示软件可以在你睡眠期间监测呼吸紊乱，并会在监测到持续性中度到重度睡眠呼吸暂停迹象时通知你。

据悉，该功能早在 2024 年便已登陆部分市场的 Apple Watch，可帮助用户识别中度至重度睡眠呼吸暂停迹象。


具体是如何识别的？苹果官方回应：基于深度学习算法及临床测试数据集构建，利用手表内置的加速感应器监测手腕细微动作以评估正常呼吸节律中断情况。


根据苹果公布的信息，支持该功能的设备包括 Apple Watch Series 9 及后续机型、Apple Watch Ultra 2 及后续机型，以及 Apple Watch SE 3。


具体操作上，将 iPhone 和手表更新至最新系统，打开 iPhone 上的健康 App，在「摘要」中找到「健康核对清单」，下滑最底部找到「移动睡眠呼吸暂停迹象提示软件」，根据指引开通即可。


需要注意的是，开通前需要确保设置过「睡眠」，并打开「通过 Apple Watch 跟踪睡眠」。


开通后，系统每 30 天会对呼吸紊乱数据进行分析。如果数据显示持续存在中度至重度睡眠呼吸暂停的迹象，用户会收到通知。需要注意的是，在为期 30 天的评估期内，必须戴着 Apple Watch 睡至少 10 晚。（来源：TechWeb）

豆包工作支持一键导入 GPT、Claude Code 技能对话，无缝切换


豆包工作正式上线数据导入同步新能力，用户可以一键把 ChatGPT、Claude Code、Trae Work 上面的技能、历史对话、工作记忆迁移过来，实现不同 AI 工具之间无缝切换。（来源：快科技）


会飞的车！特斯拉 Roadster 发布时间定档：马斯克转发预热


特斯拉官宣第二代 Roadster 将于美国时间 10 月 15 日在 SpaceX 测试基地线上直播演示，马斯克也在社交平台转发消息。

这款超跑最早于 2017 年亮相，马斯克曾提出移植 SpaceX 冷气推进技术、布置约 10 个推进器的构想，该构想可优化车辆加速表现、过弯车身姿态甚至实现短暂离地，被外界称为「会飞的跑车」。（来源：快科技）

全球首款 8K 超高清 AI 空间相机：禾赛 Kosmo One 发布，让建模像拍照一样简单


10 月 14 日现场消息，禾赛科技今日发布了「全球首款 8K 超高清 AI 空间相机」——Kosmo One，可将真实世界转化为高质量三维空间模型。

禾赛 Kosmo One 搭载一英寸 CMOS，最高拍摄分辨率可达 8K，实现 360° 无死角覆盖；15 分钟即可完成 100m² 真实空间重建，宣称「让高质量空间建模像拍照一样简单」。


禾赛 Kosmo One 可将真实世界转化为机器人训练数据，用于机器人进行物理 AI 训练，并且可用于世界模型、影视媒体、文旅文化、数字艺术等领域。


禾赛还一同发布了 Kosmo World，这是一个 AI 驱动的云平台，搭配 Kosmo One 可进行一站式 3D 内容创作与管理。（来源：IT 之家）

消息称 Nothing 将推两款智能眼镜：音频版、摄像头版，后者支持 ChatGPT


10 月 14 日消息，据消息人士 Roland Quandt 今日透露，Nothing 将推出两款智能眼镜。其中一款主打音频功能，另一款配备摄像头。

据介绍，Nothing 的音频版智能眼镜支持播放音乐、通话，用户可通过眼镜与手机的语音助手交互。该产品将配备光致变色镜片，可在阳光下自动变暗、室内自动变亮。


同时，该公司还计划推出另一款智能眼镜。该产品将拥有摄像头，支持 ChatGPT、翻译功能。


彭博社此前报道称，Nothing 的智能眼镜将通过手机和云端处理 AI 任务，不会配备 AR 显示屏。（来源：IT 之家）

因《GTA6》规模太大，Rockstar 在美国洛杉矶开设新工作室


10 月 14 日消息，据游戏媒体 Insider Gaming 今天报道，由于《GTA6》游戏规模过于庞大，Rockstar 选择在美国洛杉矶开设新工作室，进一步体现了本作的复杂程度。


R 星开发人员 Rob Nelson 对此表示，当开发团队考虑增加 NPC 数量时，很快就发现已有能力无法满足需求，最终促使公司在洛杉矶设立新工作室。


Rockstar 在洛杉矶工作室聘请了编剧、制作人、导演，专门负责打造 NPC，进一步为玩家打造鲜活、充满生机的世界。


《GTA6》将在 11 月 19 日发售，按照外界预期，《GTA6》有望打破游戏行业的多项纪录。（来源：IT 之家）

items.text:
Setting up SSH keys on macOS with Touch ID

In the first part of this post I’ll show a simple, secure way to create an SSH key on Mac (it’s 3 commands, including support for GitHub). In the second part I’ll dig deeper and explain what’s actually happening for the curious reader.

Macs have a built-in so-called Secure Enclave, where we can create “identities” that simply cannot be stolen (unless maybe you’ve made enemies with a nation state). Those identities are protected with Touch ID and can be used for SSH authentication. There are some great benefits about using this over traditional SSH key files:

The private material cannot be extracted, is never shown, cannot be stolen,

You get prompted whenever the identity is used,

No key files (like ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub and friends) littering the file system; and there’s no risk of mistakenly deleting them either.

This extra security will be in effect whenever you use SSH, including git-over-ssh like GitHub. It’s great that advanced security tech is available by default on some of the most widely distributed computers in the world! A few years ago stuff like this could only be found at CERN and/or in Dan Brown novels. Let’s see how it can be set up on your consumer-grade Mac.

It is essential that the human interface be designed for ease of use, so that users routinely and automatically apply the protection mechanisms correctly.

Saltzer and Schroeder, “The Protection of Information in Computer Systems”

Quick Setup

We’ll create a secure identity on the Secure Enclave, then tell SSH how to use it for authentication, and finally add the key to GitHub.

Step 1: create the identity that you’ll use on this Mac:

sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l ssh-key -k p-256-ne -t bio # run once to create identity

You’ll be prompted to touch “Touch ID”. Your identity is now created and saved securely (parameters are explained in the deep dive below).

Step 2: tell SSH to use the identity (when prompted for a PIN, just hit enter):

ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib # run after a reboot

From here on, SSH will know to use the identity from the Secure Enclave when connecting via SSH; it does not have a good memory so you’ll need to remind it after a reboot.

Step 3: Whenever you need to register your key to a new server (like GitHub), run this command:

ssh-add -L # run when you need the public key

If multiple identities are listed, use the line that starts with sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256.... It’s a shareable handle for the identity, and this is the SSH key that GitHub will ask about.

The output of ssh-add -L can be added as a GitHub SSH Key

That’s all you need for a super secure setup! The new identity can now be used with SSH, and you’ll be prompted for Touch ID during authentication:

git push # triggers Touch ID prompt

No one can steal your identity (well, you can’t even give it away willingly since it can’t be extracted from the Secure Enclave), but with great powers etc: if your Mac dies, so does the identity, and you’ll need to create a new one (and re-register it where necessary, like GitHub).

You’ll get a Touch ID prompt when git tries to authenticate with SSH

If you’re curious about how this works, read on!

Under the hood

We’ll now try to understand what happens under the hood. We’ll start with the actual identity creation in the Secure Enclave, then look at how SSH is allowed to interface with the Secure Enclave with ssh-keychain.dylib, and then try to see what happens in a complete SSH sign-in flow.

This is the result of reading posts (like this great investigation by arianvp), manual pages, and experimentation. A lot of this is undocumented, and this is the minimum information I needed to form a mental model of what’s happening and convince myself that it does, indeed, work.

Some of the command outputs below have been trimmed for legibility, I invite you to run them locally if you want the full experience!

Creating an identity on the Secure Enclave

Identities are managed with the sc_auth command (where sc_ stands for Smart Card). In Apple-speak, they are “CryptoTokenKit” identities, or CTK identities for short. Why not Smart Card Identities? What is a Smart Card? No idea! There’s a lot of weird Apple vocabulary, but in practice they’re just private keys stored on the Secure Enclave:

$ sc_auth list-ctk-identities
Key Type Public Key Hash Prot Label
p-256-ne 458F712F281B53C683F23FC02E69D44DAFDAA3DE bio ssh-key

If you followed along in the Quick Setup, you should have exactly one identity here, that was created when you ran the sc_auth create-ctk-identity command. Let’s look at the create-ctk-identity command in more detail:

sc_auth create-ctk-identity -l <label> -k <key type> -t <protection>

When using the p-256-ne key type, this command creates the identity on the Secure Enclave — I’m guessing by first gathering some entropy, then generating some private key material and allocating whatever it needs for bookkeeping and ensuring it can only be accessed with your fingerprint.

The label is freeform and just a note attached to the key. The key type is a cryptographic setting (the elliptic curve used). At the time of writing, the following values are accepted: p-256|p-384|p-521|p-256-ne|p-384-ne. The -ne suffix means “Non-Extractable”, meaning the key is generated by the enclave itself and cannot be extracted from the Secure Enclave. For SSH we only need signing, which is done by (and on) the Secure Enclave itself, and at no point do we need (or want) to export the private key. The p-384 curve is not supported by (Open)SSH, so this narrows it down to p-256-ne.

Finally, protection can be either bio or none. When set to bio, using the key requires biometrics (like Touch ID). With none, the key still cannot be extracted (i.e. stolen) but programs would be able to silently use SSH; I recommend using bio, but YMMV; if you get annoyed by the Touch ID prompts whenever you git pull, you might want to use none here.

Now that we have some elusive identity on the Secure Enclave, let’s see how we can tell SSH to use it for authentication.

Translating between SSH and the Secure Enclave

There’s a bit of impedance mismatch, and ssh doesn’t know how to use the identity by default:

$ ssh -T [email protected]
[email protected]: Permission denied (publickey).

The SSH agent cannot use the Secure Enclave identities as-is, but Apple has us covered with a small translation layer in the form of ssh-keychain.dylib, a dlopen-able library available natively on all recent macOS versions:

$ ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
...
Resident identity added: ECDSA-SK SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w

Here we’re relying on ssh-add’s built-in support for FIDO-style authenticator via the -K parameter. This lets the SSH agent know that it shouldn’t read a standard private key (for instance ~/.ssh/id_ed25519) but that it should expect the keys to be stored “externally” (for a lack of better words). With -K alone, ssh-add would look for public keys on USB devices (think YubiKey); though we can customize this behavior by registering a “security key provider” with -S <provider>. This provider should be a stateless dynamically-loadable library, which is exactly what /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib is. The interface is not documented (at least not in a way I was able to meaningfully process), but we can have a look at what ssh-keychain.dylib exposes:

$ dyld_info -exports /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
/usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib:
-exports:
offset symbol
0x00001A2C _C_GetFunctionList
0x00000F30 _sk_api_version
0x00000F38 _sk_enroll
0x0000136C _sk_load_resident_keys
0x00000F40 _sk_sign

Most likely, _sk_load_resident_keys is meant to return a list of (public keys of) identities, and _sk_sign will sign a payload using a specified identity (here, resident means “residing on e.g. the Secure Enclave”).

We’ve seen how the identities can be created on the Secure Enclave, and how they can, in theory, be used by the SSH agent. Let’s put this to the test and see what happens when an SSH connection is created.

SSH Sign-in flow with the ssh-keychain provider

Let’s see what we need for authenticating to a remote SSH server. At all times, the SSH agent needs (1) a list of (public) keys that can be used to authenticate, and (2) a way to prove to a server that it has the corresponding private key for any of those keys.

When ssh-add is first called with -S <provider>, the _sk_load_resident_keys routine is called, which returns the public keys of all resident keys on the FIDO-style authenticator. Those are stored in the SSH agent (alongside their corresponding provider, namely ssh-keychain.dylib) and will later be offered as candidates to any remote SSH server we try connecting to. (Also now that the SSH agent knows about the Secure Enclave identity we created earlier, we can view its SSH-style public key with ssh-add -L.)

Let’s say an SSH connection is initiated: the remote accepts one of those public keys offered by the agent and “challenges” the client to prove its identity. The agent calls _sk_sign to create a signature with the private key (matching the accepted public key) and the challenge (roughly speaking). This will be forwarded to the Secure Enclave, prompt Touch ID, and if approved, will return a signature for the challenge. The signature is forwarded back to the server, which can confirm we — the client — have the corresponding private key.

Let’s see what this looks like in practice:

$ ssh -T [email protected]
[email protected]: Permission denied (publickey).
$ ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
Enter PIN for authenticator:
Resident identity added: ...
$ ssh -vvv -T [email protected]
debug1: get_agent_identities: agent returned 1 keys
debug1: Offering public key: ssh: ECDSA-SK SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w authenticator agent
debug1: Server accepts key: ssh: ECDSA-SK SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w authenticator agent
debug3: sign_and_send_pubkey: signing using [email protected] SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w
<at this point, Touch ID prompt appears>
Authenticated to github.com ([20.250.119.67]:22) using "publickey".
Hi nmattia! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.

The ssh debug logs show that one key is offered by the agent, accepted, and then used to create a signature. After the server has verified the signature, authentication is granted (although GitHub does not provide shell access).

One note: whenever we register the identity with the SSH agent, ssh-add prompts us for a PIN. What gives? Why does entering an empty PIN work, isn’t this mighty unsafe‽

Well, no, it’s not unsafe! When we tell ssh-add to use a FIDO-style authenticator, I suspect its default behavior is to ask for a PIN as it assumes we’ll be using a USB, YubiKey-style authenticator; only we shortcut the whole thing with ssh-keychain.dylib (and the security comes not from a PIN, but from the soft skin under your fingertips; much cooler). Not great in terms of usability, but I guess it makes sense. (I have no idea what would happen if you have more than one FIDO authenticator; go support me on GitHub and I’ll buy a collection of YubiKeys to experiment).

Conclusion

Let’s recap: we can use a somewhat cryptic, poorly documented “Smart Card” tool to create a “CryptoTokenKit” identity on the “Secure Enclave”. Then, by using the poorly documented ssh-keychain.dylib, we can use said identity to generate signatures that Apple’s ssh can use. There’s no guarantee that all this missing documentation wouldn’t say “Do not use this; terribly unsafe in practice”, but hey: all this security talk by Apple, they wouldn’t lie to us, right? *spooky*

Joke aside, it’s pretty cool to have sci-fi style security modules baked into most modern devices; the more people start using them and pushing for openness, the better the support from the companies will be. We can have nice things!

Again, a lot of this was derived from this gist; highly recommend having a read and potentially asking questions in the discussion.

Let me knoworjoin the discussion if you enjoyed this article! You can also subscribe to receive updates.

Let’s say an SSH connection is initiated: the remote accepts one of those public keys offered by the agent and “challenges” the client to prove its identity. The agent calls _sk_sign to create a signature with the private key (matching the accepted public key) and the challenge (roughly speaking). This will be forwarded to the Secure Enclave, prompt Touch ID, and if approved, will return a signature for the challenge. The signature is forwarded back to the server, which can confirm we — the client — have the corresponding private key.
Let’s see what this looks like in practice:

$ ssh -T [email protected]
[email protected]: Permission denied (publickey).
$ ssh-add -K -S /usr/lib/ssh-keychain.dylib
Enter PIN for authenticator:
Resident identity added: ...
$ ssh -vvv -T [email protected]
debug1: get_agent_identities: agent returned 1 keys
debug1: Offering public key: ssh: ECDSA-SK SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w authenticator agent
debug1: Server accepts key: ssh: ECDSA-SK SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w authenticator agent
debug3: sign_and_send_pubkey: signing using [email protected] SHA256:QZ+Cx6/AkS9sek9INtsXt6t7wuHOtA555CLJu8a8V7w
<at this point, Touch ID prompt appears>
Authenticated to github.com ([20.250.119.67]:22) using "publickey".
Hi nmattia! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.

The ssh debug logs show that one key is offered by the agent, accepted, and then used to create a signature. After the server has verified the signature, authentication is granted (although GitHub does not provide shell access).
One note: whenever we register the identity with the SSH agent, ssh-add prompts us for a PIN. What gives? Why does entering an empty PIN work, isn’t this mighty unsafe‽

Well, no, it’s not unsafe! When we tell ssh-add to use a FIDO-style authenticator, I suspect its default behavior is to ask for a PIN as it assumes we’ll be using a USB, YubiKey-style authenticator; only we shortcut the whole thing with ssh-keychain.dylib (and the security comes not from a PIN, but from the soft skin under your fingertips; much cooler). Not great in terms of usability, but I guess it makes sense. (I have no idea what would happen if you have more than one FIDO authenticator; go support me on GitHub and I’ll buy a collection of YubiKeys to experiment).
Conclusion

Let’s recap: we can use a somewhat cryptic, poorly documented “Smart Card” tool to create a “CryptoTokenKit” identity on the “Secure Enclave”. Then, by using the poorly documented ssh-keychain.dylib, we can use said identity to generate signatures that Apple’s ssh can use. There’s no guarantee that all this missing documentation wouldn’t say “Do not use this; terribly unsafe in practice”, but hey: all this security talk by Apple, they wouldn’t lie to us, right? *spooky*

Joke aside, it’s pretty cool to have sci-fi style security modules baked into most modern devices; the more people start using them and pushing for openness, the better the support from the companies will be. We can have nice things!
Again, a lot of this was derived from this gist; highly recommend having a read and potentially asking questions in the discussion.
Let me knoworjoin the discussion if you enjoyed this article! You can also subscribe to receive updates.

items.title: Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code
items.author: dnw
items.summary:
Chris Rohlf

Over the past year, we’ve published lots of data that shows that frontier AI models are more than capable of discovering and exploiting security
items.text:
Chris Rohlf

Over the past year, we’ve published lots of data that shows that frontier AI models are more than capable of discovering and exploiting security vulnerabilities. Showing how previously unknown vulnerabilities might be exploited is, however, only the start of what frontier AI models can do for cyber defense. In this post, we summarize some of our initial research into automated attack surface analysis and reduction: the process of using AI models to map the code that is reachable, then removing or restricting access to anything than a given deployment doesn’t need to expose.

Automated attack surface analysis and reduction can meaningfully improve the security of deployed software in the near term. Securing software by finding and fixing individual vulnerabilities alone scales poorly: fixing even a critical vulnerability tells you nothing about the vulnerabilities that remain. By contrast, reducing code reachability can reduce the severity of unknown vulnerabilities, including the ones that might be under active exploitation. These techniques don’t remove the unknown vulnerabilities in the code, but they do make the vulnerabilities harder to reach, and thereby reduce their severity. Minimizing codebases’ attack surface results in better security without ever having to find or fix an individual vulnerability.

Below, we preview some of the data we’ve collected from applying attack surface reduction techniques to large open-source codebases using Claude. Our aim in doing so is to show that Claude can meaningfully, and economically, improve software security through the methods we outline. Specifically, we ran Claude over 25 projects (in a variety of languages), and it discovered 493 issues. With these results in mind, we discuss how developers can apply similar techniques to their own code.

Methods for reducing codebases’ attack surface

Over time, software has a tendency to become more complicated, with new layers of abstractions, new dependencies, and new features slowly piling on top of one-another. This can often cause it to function very differently to how its original developers intended. And it is a big part of why attackers are often so successful: they study exactly how a piece of code behaves in practice, rather than how its developers intended or designed it to work.

Automated attack surface analysis and reduction techniques aim to discover unnecessary attack surfaces, then move that code behind an appropriate gate. This might involve moving code from pre-authentication to post-authentication, from 0-click to 1-click, from on-by-default to explicit opt-in, or from the first message of a protocol to deeper in the session state machine. Some code is meant to be reachable before these stages, but a lot it is not, and, given the complexity that comes with code churn across thousands or millions of lines of code, unnecessary exposure of features often goes unnoticed.

There are numerous ways to reduce the attack surface of code. In our own research efforts, we focused on three methods in particular:

Default configuration. We identified code that was reachable in its shipped default configuration but wasn’t intended to be used by any default functionality.

Configuration interaction. We found pairs of options that looked reasonable on their own, but which caused issues when configured together (for instance, by silently disabling a security control, or leaving a features behavior undefined while its code remains reachable).

Early reachability. We identified security sensitive and complex code that runs either before an appropriate security control (such as authentication), without victim interaction, or before a protocol state transition.

We wanted to understand how well Claude could take these three descriptions of attack surface and discover real issues in large and complex codebases. We analyzed 25 open source projects (representing over five million lines of code), written in languages including C, C++, Java, PHP, and Python. Claude created an inventory of over 17,000 configuration options across these projects. Of those, 3,842 related to the configuration of a control or feature that was security relevant.

For the purposes of our research, we broke down these open source projects into three broad categories:

Public. These projects are built to serve any user who can reach them, or to consume data authored by parties they cannot identify. (Examples include a DNS resolver parsing upstream answers, or a proxy parsing origin responses.)

Gated. These projects are intended to serve authenticated users (such as those with a password, key or certificate holders, or enrolled devices). The software still allows for arbitrary client requests, but no functionality is available until the user has been authenticated.

Private. These are built and deployed to serve the operator's own private environment. In these cases, adding a control like an authentication layer is optional, but outside the scope of the software.

These categories help to contextualize our results. For example, we’d expect a significant percentage of a Public codebase to be reachable in the default configuration (since it’s designed to serve any user), but the opposite to be true for projects in the Gated category.

Claude’s findings

Claude found 493 issues using the three methods described above. Several themes stuck out to us from its results.

First, Claude found that all eleven gated projects had code that was unintentionally reachable (although this code wasn’t a significant percentage of the total lines of code for any of those projects). Specifically, Claude discovered 93 unnecessary pre-authentication surfaces in the default configuration of the gated cohort, 37 locations where code executed, or state was recorded, before authentication, and 61 configuration combinations that silently weakened a pre-authentication control configured by the administrator. None of these issues would have been immediately exploitable on their own, but they create a much larger attack surface than is necessary.

Second, Claude’s work mitigating configuration interaction issues produced some of the most interesting and impactful findings (across all project types). Claude found 162 security sensitive configuration combinations that were accepted both without an error or warning and without any documentation of the expected behavior of their interaction. In 94 of those cases, the combination silently turned off a security control. The other 68 cases were inconsistencies in the same security mechanisms (e.g. a listener or login path would remain reachable even though the configuration would say it was disabled; two settings would conflict, and the one that would take precedence would depend on their order in the configuration file, or a protection configured by the administrator would do nothing while its code remained reachable). While some of these configuration combinations might be non-standard or infrequently used, there would be nothing preventing an administrator of these projects from configuring and deploying the code in this way.

Claude also found one specific pattern that turned up independently in four unrelated projects. This would work as follows. An administrator would write an access rule for remote clients using a hostname or a wildcard pattern, instead of an IP address. When a client connects, the server would compare that rule against the client’s hostname. Whether the server ever learned that hostname would depend on a separate option that controlled reverse DNS lookups (which most projects had configured off). With lookups off, the server would only have the client’s IP address. The server would compare the rule against that address as plain text. But a hostname pattern can never match an IP address. This means that a deny rule would never fire, and the list would fail open. Some of the affected projects mention in their documentation that hostname rules depend on DNS lookups being enabled, but none state that a deny list written this way would have fail open behavior.

Third, Claude often discovered that two configuration options would conflict in a way that silently dropped a security check. In one case, an administrator could require every connecting client to prove its identity with a certificate. In another, the code was only intended to delay that check until it was required, but in fact disabled the check entirely. A server that was configured to accept only trusted clients would therefore accept a connection from anyone. This exposed a large body of request handling code (which was supposed to be behind the certificate check) to unauthenticated clients. The software accepted both configuration options together with no warning under default settings; the documentation never mentioned that the certificate requirement had been dropped. This conflicting set of configuration options had been present in the software for 21 years.

Finally, Claude discovered an issue in a project that left authentication off by default (and expected the administrator to turn it on). The option that required TLS client certificates was honored on most of the project’s network endpoints, but silently ignored on a few others (ones which loaded their TLS settings through a path with a different namespace). This meant that a client with no certificate could complete the TLS handshake and open a session on an affected endpoint. Nothing would be logged about the ignored setting. Whether the option takes effect would depend on the namespace used by the administrator in the configuration. One form of the setting name works on every endpoint, but the shorter form—which most examples use—is dropped on the affected ones.

Case study: OpenSSH

Surprisingly, when measured as a percentage of the total lines of code, the project for which Claude achieved the largest reduction in attack surface was OpenSSH. OpenSSH is a high quality C codebase that provides secure remote access. Claude traced the input paths of the SSH daemon in the 10.4 release and found roughly 4,500 lines of new and experimental code for ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum signature algorithm, that an unauthenticated client could reach in the default configuration. ML-DSA is not enabled by default, but the code was reachable regardless, even when an administrator explicitly excluded the algorithm. The daemon parsed whichever key type the client sent, (and, for certificates, it also verified the embedded CA signature). Only then did it check whether that key type was allowed. There is no good reason for this complex, memory unsafe code to be reachable when it hasn’t been enabled by the configuration. Those 4,500 lines of code in ML-DSA-44 are about 16% of OpenSSH’s own pre-authentication code in a default sshd. We reported this to the OpenSSH developers along with patches. The 10.5 release moved the check before parsing.

Claude then noted two gaps in the 10.5 check. The first was a mismatch between what the client claimed and what it sent. The check looked at the algorithm name advertised by the client, but the parser was chosen by a type string embedded inside the key blob. A client could advertise ssh-ed25519, pass the check, and still send an ML-DSA key that would be parsed.

The second gap was in the 10.5 check’s certificates. Certificate key types were enabled by default. Given a certificate supplied by an attacker, sshd would deserialize the embedded CA public key and run a full signature verification with it, for any supported algorithm, before consulting the configuration. The user key signature path was properly gated behind the list of public keys allowed to connect to the server, but the CA signature path was not. That made every public key signature verifier in the binary reachable by any client that could complete a key exchange. We built a proof of concept and worked through several iterations of a fix with the maintainers. The resulting change placed the checks inside the parser itself. The encoded key type and the certificate’s CA signature algorithm are now compared against the configured allow lists before the corresponding deserialization or signature verification.

This fix removed roughly a fifth of the OpenSSH code that an unauthenticated client previously could have reached in a default build. Almost all of that was the new ML-DSA code, which is now unreachable even for a client that lies about its key type or hides an ML-DSA CA key inside an otherwise acceptable certificate. Certificates signed with an allowed CA algorithm are still parsed and verified, but the check now runs before parsing. The maintainers shipped the changes described here in version 10.6.

OpenSSH is some of the most heavily audited code in the world. If unnecessary reachability survives there, it can survive anywhere. This suggests that reducing the attack surface of codebases is likely to pay dividends across many important codebases.

Conclusion

It is perhaps impossible to measure how many unknown vulnerabilities are in any given codebase. And there is plenty of data that shows attackers can and will find those vulnerabilities with enough time (particularly if equipped with frontier AI models). But a defender who reduces unnecessary attack surface in their code reduces the risk from all of the unknown vulnerabilities in that code at once—including any that are already being quietly exploited. OpenSSH is some of the most audited C code in the world. Yet it shipped around 4,500 lines of experimental signature parsing code that could have been reached by an attacker prior to any configuration check.

We have combined the attack surface reduction techniques we described above into one reusable Claude skill, which we are working to integrate into OSS-Scanner. The skill runs three passes on a codebase. Each time it starts fresh (with an empty context window), except for a short piece of context it receives from the prior pass.

In the first pass, the skill looks at whether there is code that the default configuration allows to be reached but which isn’t used by any intended functionality. In the second pass, it looks at the code that runs before any hard gates (like authentication) or before protocol state machine entry points, in any configuration. Finally, third, the skill assesses which combinations of configurations silently switch a security control off or degrade its efficacy. In every pass, Claude creates an inventory of the entry points from the code and confirms each finding with a dynamic trace of the program. For default configuration findings, it designs and implements a gate and ensures that this causes no change in the program’s default behavior. It does so by running the project's own test suite (along with a black box regression suite) against the baseline; it requires modified builds to have identical results. Any gate that would change a non-default configuration is set aside for a human to decide. For the other two passes, it proposes changes like reordering a configuration check, adding a guard to enforce state ordering, or rejecting the combination at configuration load. Even without using this specific skill, we think the broad methodology outlined here is likely to be effective.

The techniques outlined in this post offer only a very limited view into what is possible in attack surface reduction. For instance, Claude is also capable of analyzing and comparing runtime logs against configurations to ensure that only required functionality has been enabled: disabling unused parsers, legacy protocols, and dashboards reduces security risk at little cost.

We encourage organizations to explore using Claude to analyze and reduce the attack surface of the software they depend on. We expect this to be one of the most practical ways that developers can measurably improve the security of the code the world already runs on.

items.title: 曝高通启动全球裁员；上线 40 天，Muse 下载量突破 1000 万次；ChatGPT 上线幻灯片工具
items.summary:
DeepSeek 开源大规模云服务推理框架


10 月 20 日下午，DeepSeek 宣布，在此前开源一系列大模型、TileLang 编译工具及推理算子库的基础上，决定进一步将内部推理框架 DeepInfer 全面开源。


DeepSeek 称，基于 DeepInfer，已实现 DeepSeek V4.1
items.text:
DeepSeek 开源大规模云服务推理框架


10 月 20 日下午，DeepSeek 宣布，在此前开源一系列大模型、TileLang 编译工具及推理算子库的基础上，决定进一步将内部推理框架 DeepInfer 全面开源。


DeepSeek 称，基于 DeepInfer，已实现 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 高吞吐、低延迟的大规模推理服务。未来，DeepSeek 新模型的推理代码及后续优化也将在此持续更新。


券有商分析师认为，开源模型与 Agent 工具链的持续完善，有望降低应用开发成本，推动 AICoding 向游戏开发、3D 内容制作、企业软件及自动化工作流等场景扩展，具备开发者入口和应用生态的平台有望优先受益。（来源：证券时报）

上线 40 天，Muse 下载量突破 1000 万


市场情报机构 Sensor Tower 的最新数据显示，Meta 的人工智能助手 Muse 自 9 月推出以来，累计下载量达 1090 万次，其中美国地区下载量为 1020 万次。


迄今为止仅有另外 11 款应用达成过这一上线后的里程碑，上一款实现该成绩的正是 Meta 的 Threads，时间为 2023 年 7 月。


另据数据显示，Muse 的用户留存表现优于 ChatGPT、Claude、Grok 等 AI 竞品。（来源：IT之家）

华为引望、宁德时代合作换电车型拟 2027 年上市


10 月 20 日，媒体报道称华为引望与宁德时代、时代电服合作正推进首批车型的开发，涉及五款新车，计划 2027 年上市。有报道表示，首款采用巧克力换电的车型为东风与华为合作的奕境品牌旗下产品。


引望成立于 2024 年，承接华为原智能汽车解决方案业务，向车企提供智能驾驶、智能座舱、车控等系统及部件。


而宁德时代正在通过技术合作、股权投资等方式扩大换电业务规模。赛豆科技旗下 AIVA 品牌首款量产车 AIVA ME7 将采用换电模式，宁德时代提供电池技术及充换电体系支持，具体方案还在规划中。（来源：晚点 Auto、财联社）

曝高通将启动全球裁员


据路透社报道，高通 CEO 克里斯蒂亚诺·安蒙近期在一份内部备忘录中告知员工，公司将在年度员工评估后，开展以绩效为重点的全球裁员，相关通知将于 11 月开始发出。


安蒙表示，此举旨在建立更强的绩效文化，并解决公司持续未能达到预期的情况。备忘录未披露裁员人数，路透社也暂时无法确定此次裁员的规模。


路透社在报道中指出作为全球最大的智能手机芯片制造商之一，高通今年受到消费电子产品销售低迷的冲击，存储芯片价格飙升抑制了关键市场的需求。


随着业务向快速增长的 AI 数据中心市场拓展，高通预计，2027 财年，公司芯片销售收入的大部分将来自智能手机以外的业务。（来源：凤凰网科技）

C919 大飞机国产发动机将进入取证试飞阶段


日前，网友爆料称，运 20 飞行台上挂载了国产自研大飞机 C919 的国产替代发动机 CJ1000A 开始试飞了，推测应该该发动机进入了取证试飞阶段。


航发科技公司上周在互动平台上回应过 CJ1000A 的进展，表示公司承制的 CJ 1000A 发动机相关零部件设计构型及工艺路线已实现初步冻结，后续不排除根据 TC Only 批次制造符合性检查开展情况、总师单位取证试验结果发生局部调整优化的可能。


CJ1000A 发动机的目标是实现 C919 现有发动机 LEAP-1C 的替代，这就意味着需要在动力、经济、维护等方面看齐 LEAP-1C。


报道表示：考虑到 LEAP-1C 是当前最先进的商用发动机之一，CJ1000A 的难度可想而知，所以这也是这款发动机打磨了 10 多年的原因，需要每个环节都要做到可靠稳定。明年能拿证就很乐观了，正式运营可能还要等到 28-29 年。（来源：快科技）

杨立昆吐槽特斯拉飞行汽车不实用，马斯克回怼：「放屁」


人工智能先驱人物、AMI Labs 创始人兼董事长杨立昆（Yann LeCun）最近在 X 平台点评了特斯拉刚刚发布的「飞行汽车」Roadster，认为这款产品「完全不实用」。


杨立昆表示，这辆汽车用的只是压缩空气，比冲很差（不到 50 秒）。即使假设压缩空气占整车质量的 50%，在推重比大于 1.0 的情况下，有效推力也只能维持不到 10 秒，实际上可能只有 5 秒左右。


因此他表示，这辆车肯定只是一个空心的轻量化外壳，加上大型压缩空气罐。发布会很有意思，但产品完全不实用。


马斯克对此回应称：「我冲着你的方向放了个屁。」

而杨立昆则回怼道：「如果腹部压力足够大，放屁确实可能让你飞起来。仔细想想，你的汽车也是靠同样原理驱动的：一个压力高达 700 bar、容量 600 升、持续 3 秒、声音巨大的屁。【希望里面没有甲烷，和那些臭得要死的化合物】。」（来源：IT之家）

《GTA 6》数字版预购突破 600 万份，销售额接近 6 亿美元

距离正式发售仍有一个多月时间，Rockstar Games 备受期待的开放世界大作《侠盗猎车手 6》（GTA 6）已经展现出惊人的市场号召力。


根据市场分析机构 Sensor Tower 最新估算，截至 10 月 13 日，该游戏全球数字版预购量已突破 600 万份，预计带来约 5.94 亿美元收入，成为近年来游戏行业最受瞩目的预售产品之一。


报告还显示，高价版本成为玩家购买主力。售价 100 美元的 Ultimate Edition 终极版占据绝大多数预购份额。即便单独统计这一高端版本，其销售曲线依然远高于近年来任何同类游戏产品。（来源：cnBeta）

理想宣布电池保障计划：电池不自燃、碰撞不起火终身保障


10 月 20 日，在理想汽车 Power Day 电动技术发布会上，理想正式发布完整自研三电技术体系「连山」。


同时，理想推出「连山电池保障计划」，提供双重终身保障：一是「电池不自燃终身保障」，因原厂电池质量问题导致自燃且车辆达到报废条件，补偿同等配置新车；二是「碰撞不起火终身保障」，因碰撞或底盘剐蹭导致起火且达到报废条件，补偿车损险保单额与保险实际赔付金额差额。（来源：凤凰网科技）

马斯克股权薪酬曝光，为员工中位数 250 万倍


据福布斯报道，特斯拉当地时间周一向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交的 14A 代理声明文件显示，公司 CEO 马斯克 2025 年从特斯拉获得的薪酬总额约 1,584 亿美元（约合 1.06 万亿元人民币），其中 CEO 绩效奖励最高价值 1,323 亿美元、临时奖励价值 261 亿美元。


基于超过 13 万名符合统计条件员工的数据，2025 年特斯拉非高管普通员工的薪酬中位数为 6.27 万美元（约合 42 万元人民币），该数字高于 2024 年的 5.72 万美元，但和马斯克 2025 年薪酬相比，仅为后者的 250 万分之一还不到。


文件说明，马斯克在特斯拉的薪酬全部为股权形式，只有当公司达成预设业绩目标，他才能全额拿到奖励。（来源：IT之家）

OpenAI 上线 ChatGPT Slides 幻灯片工具，支持团队协作

OpenAI 于上月发布了 ChatGPT Space，配套包含 Pages、Slides、Sheets 等工具。该公司当时表示，Slides 和 Sheets 会在后续推出。几周之后，OpenAI 终于在 ChatGPT 中上线了 Slides（幻灯片工具）。


ChatGPT 官方账号在 X 平台发文，公布现已可用的多项 ChatGPT Slides 功能。用户现在可以让 ChatGPT 基于对话内容、上传文件或者大纲生成演示文稿，也可以直接选用多款内置模板来创建。


演示文稿生成完成后，用户可以像在谷歌幻灯片（Google Slides）中一样与团队分享。被邀请的用户能够实时协同编辑文稿、修改内容并留下评论反馈。用户还可以指令 ChatGPT，根据团队反馈自动调整幻灯片。


ChatGPT Slides 现已面向 Pro、Business 以及 Enterprise 套餐用户开放，Plus 用户目前无法使用该功能。（来源：IT之家）

影翎无人机推出经典遥控器、4G 图传增强模块两款配件

10 月 20 日，影翎为 A1 全景无人机推出两款全新配件，经典遥控器加上 4G 图传增强模块组合，到手售价 699 元，限时 8 折促销价 559 元。


这套配件里面的经典遥控器采用双摇杆布局，和传统无人机操控手感接近。可以在固定视角、自由视角两种模式来回切换，精细调整飞行轨迹，做复杂运镜拍摄的时候，操控精度会更高。


另一件重点配件是 4G 图传增强模块，内置 eSIM，不用额外插实体 SIM 卡就可以直接使用。


无人机原生无线图传遇到楼房、山体遮挡，信号容易出现卡顿，这个模块会自动切换蜂窝网络补位，在城市高楼或者山谷这类复杂环境，尽可能稳住图传画面，减少卡顿黑屏问题。新品限时赠送 5GB 流量，首年免收服务费。（来源：快科技）

部分用户借助 AI 清除智能电视广告及预装应用


根据外媒报道，近日部分开发者和普通用户开始借助 Claude Code 等 AI 工具，对智能电视中的广告和预装软件进行清理、禁用追踪功能，以减少广告干扰并改善操作流畅度。


其中一个名为 CleanYourTV 的项目由开发者 Gathin T. 发起。他将父母使用的电视型号提供给 Claude Code，后者通过 Wi-Fi 连接电视，禁用了 25 个原生软件包，并生成了一个新的启动器，将原本的电视主屏幕替换为更简洁的界面。


Gathin T. 随后公开了相关提示词和项目代码，并称接下来两天有数千名用户尝试在自己的设备上进行类似改造。


除使用现成项目外，还有用户直接让 AI 编程智能体协助修改电视系统。X 用户 Ryan Doyle 于 10 月 17 日分享称，他向 Claude Code 提供电视产品信息并询问能否修改设备，随后按照其引导移除了广告和部分预装软件，调整了屏幕保护程序，并改善了界面响应速度。（来源：IT之家）

10 月 20 日下午，DeepSeek 宣布，在此前开源一系列大模型、TileLang 编译工具及推理算子库的基础上，决定进一步将内部推理框架 DeepInfer 全面开源。
DeepSeek 称，基于 DeepInfer，已实现 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 高吞吐、低延迟的大规模推理服务。未来，DeepSeek 新模型的推理代码及后续优化也将在此持续更新。
券有商分析师认为，开源模型与 Agent 工具链的持续完善，有望降低应用开发成本，推动 AICoding 向游戏开发、3D 内容制作、企业软件及自动化工作流等场景扩展，具备开发者入口和应用生态的平台有望优先受益。（来源：证券时报）
上线 40 天，Muse 下载量突破 1000 万
市场情报机构 Sensor Tower 的最新数据显示，Meta 的人工智能助手 Muse 自 9 月推出以来，累计下载量达 1090 万次，其中美国地区下载量为 1020 万次。
迄今为止仅有另外 11 款应用达成过这一上线后的里程碑，上一款实现该成绩的正是 Meta 的 Threads，时间为 2023 年 7 月。
另据数据显示，Muse 的用户留存表现优于 ChatGPT、Claude、Grok 等 AI 竞品。（来源：IT之家）
华为引望、宁德时代合作换电车型拟 2027 年上市
10 月 20 日，媒体报道称华为引望与宁德时代、时代电服合作正推进首批车型的开发，涉及五款新车，计划 2027 年上市。有报道表示，首款采用巧克力换电的车型为东风与华为合作的奕境品牌旗下产品。
引望成立于 2024 年，承接华为原智能汽车解决方案业务，向车企提供智能驾驶、智能座舱、车控等系统及部件。
而宁德时代正在通过技术合作、股权投资等方式扩大换电业务规模。赛豆科技旗下 AIVA 品牌首款量产车 AIVA ME7 将采用换电模式，宁德时代提供电池技术及充换电体系支持，具体方案还在规划中。（来源：晚点 Auto、财联社）
曝高通将启动全球裁员
据路透社报道，高通 CEO 克里斯蒂亚诺·安蒙近期在一份内部备忘录中告知员工，公司将在年度员工评估后，开展以绩效为重点的全球裁员，相关通知将于 11 月开始发出。
安蒙表示，此举旨在建立更强的绩效文化，并解决公司持续未能达到预期的情况。备忘录未披露裁员人数，路透社也暂时无法确定此次裁员的规模。
路透社在报道中指出作为全球最大的智能手机芯片制造商之一，高通今年受到消费电子产品销售低迷的冲击，存储芯片价格飙升抑制了关键市场的需求。
随着业务向快速增长的 AI 数据中心市场拓展，高通预计，2027 财年，公司芯片销售收入的大部分将来自智能手机以外的业务。（来源：凤凰网科技）

航发科技公司上周在互动平台上回应过 CJ1000A 的进展，表示公司承制的 CJ 1000A 发动机相关零部件设计构型及工艺路线已实现初步冻结，后续不排除根据 TC Only 批次制造符合性检查开展情况、总师单位取证试验结果发生局部调整优化的可能。
CJ1000A 发动机的目标是实现 C919 现有发动机 LEAP-1C 的替代，这就意味着需要在动力、经济、维护等方面看齐 LEAP-1C。
报道表示：考虑到 LEAP-1C 是当前最先进的商用发动机之一，CJ1000A 的难度可想而知，所以这也是这款发动机打磨了 10 多年的原因，需要每个环节都要做到可靠稳定。明年能拿证就很乐观了，正式运营可能还要等到 28-29 年。（来源：快科技）

自从马斯克推出了「会飞的特斯拉」之后，网上出现了一批又一批的梗图，比如飞越收费站、跳起来躲开隔壁弹出来的电池，甚至带着李有田飞下悬崖。

但玩笑过后，更多人开始思考，这辆 Roadster 到底能干嘛？它到底算不算飞行汽车？


美国哥伦比亚广播公司找上美国联邦航空管理局（FAA），提了一个很关键的问题：这台能在天上翻跟头的交通工具到底归谁管。他们得到的答复是：


特斯拉 Roadster 不符合 FAA 对航空器的定义。


美国国家公路交通安全管理局随后表态，即便这辆车在视觉上挑战了物理定律，特斯拉也必须保证它符合适用的机动车安全标准，驾驶员同样要遵守属地道路法规。


意思就是：Roadster 并不是一辆飞行汽车。

要解释清楚这件事，得先来看看这辆号称使用了火箭技术的跑车，是怎么离开地面的。


特斯拉能飞，但只能飞六秒


发布会上的画面让人眼花缭乱，但真要讲起来其实很简单。特斯拉一共用了两套方案：一套负责把车吸在跑道上，另一套负责把车推向半空。


Roadster 倒挂在跑道顶端的关键，在于车底那几台大功率风扇。

就在发布会举行两周之前，美国专利商标局通过了特斯拉的一项新专利。从这份代号 US 12,377,920 B1 的专利文件里可以看到，特斯拉在后扩散器的位置布置了 4 台电动涵道风扇。


据特斯拉介绍，这 4 台轴流风扇的单台功率在 20 kW 左右，电机架构源自特斯拉成熟的热泵压缩机。

与之配合的是底盘边缘的主动密封裙边，这些裙边能够随路面起伏活动，把车底的空间隔离出来。当车辆开上跑道时，风扇会迅速抽空车底与路面之间的空气，形成局部负压，让车子始终紧贴跑道。


自然地，这几个风扇对过弯也有帮助。


特斯拉车辆工程副总裁拉尔斯·莫拉维透露，在时速 0 到 50 英里（约 80km/h）的低速状态下，这套负压系统能够提供超过 2G 的横向抓地力。

让 Roadster 在脱离跑道后跃入空中的，是车内另一套来自航天领域的方案。


在现场演示特技的 Rocket 版本里，工程师拆掉了副驾驶座椅，塞进了一个容量达到 600 升的碳纤维缠绕高压储气罐。这个气罐承受着 700 bar 的高压，里面储存了将近 250 公斤的高压气体。

这些高压气体会顺着管路分流到全车 10 个喷嘴，其中车尾的 4 个是负责纵向加速的主喷嘴，车底四角各有一个垂直推力喷嘴，车身两侧还布置了姿态微调阀门。


莫拉维还提到，为了让各喷嘴在喷出高压气体时不出现时间差，工程师们在底盘下做了一组严格等长的管路布局。

他强调，即便各喷嘴之间的气流只慢了千分之几秒，也会让已经起跳的车辆瞬间失去平衡。


总结下来，全新 Roadster 跳起来的流程大概就是：


底部的垂直喷嘴开启，高压气体向地面喷出，产生超过车身重力的反作用力，把车体托入空中。紧接着，车侧喷嘴点火，车载陀螺仪计算角速度，在车身刚好翻转 180° 的瞬间喷出反向气流制动，随后着陆。

诚然，整套动作在视觉上是足够科幻的，但这仍然够不着 FAA 对于「飞行器」的定义。


根据美国联邦法规，能够依靠空气动力或动力升力，在空域中维持受控的巡航与导航的，才能算作航空器。Roadster 显然达不到这个要求，原因很简单，它的推进系统最多就只能撑几秒钟。


航天领域常用「比冲」来衡量推力效率，简单来说就是看推进剂能顶多长时间。普通火箭靠化学燃料做功，比冲通常在 300 秒以上，而特斯拉采用的冷气推进由于没有热量释放，比冲一般被卡在 50 秒上下。


比冲低，说明气体喷出的流速不够快，想要达到足够大的推力，就只能提升喷气量。

而维持一台接近 1.8 吨的 Roadster 悬停，需要产生接近 18000 牛的持续推力。按照理论公式换算，这套系统每秒钟必须向外喷出大约 35 公斤的气体。


也就是说，储气罐里装下的 250 公斤气体，在全推力工况下，撑不过 6 秒钟。


据海外媒体 MotorTrend 报道，现场完成三次跳跃的演示车辆，储气量刚好是普通的 Thrust 推进版本的三倍——后者的储气罐只有 200 升，在全推力工况下，甚至撑不过 2 秒，后续的充气时间则长达 6 到 7 个小时。

即便退一步把它当成一辆普通汽车，现有的设计想要通过道路安全认证也困难重重，马斯克自己大概也清楚这一点。在发布会后，特斯拉在官网上干脆写明，这辆能飞的 Rocket 版本「尚未获准在公共道路上行驶」，甚至采用了极少见的邀请制发售。


「安全不是主要目标。比如你买一辆法拉利，安全不会是首要目标。如果安全是你的首要目标，我会说别买 Roadster。」马斯克说。

对一台百万美元的极客玩具来说，马斯克或许可以把安全放在次要位置。但对于任何面向公众出行的交通工具而言，安全从来都是不可逾越的红线。国内造车新势力里同样在探索飞行汽车的何小鹏，在看完发布会后给出了一段评价。


能否落地还要看飞行安全，飞行参数等具体指标。但是所有人都无法绕开飞行认证，在全球这都是需要一个长期工作。


何小鹏所说的飞行认证，是所有低空载人交通工具必须跨过的制度门槛。从适航审定到航线划设，每一步都需要长期的验证。


在社交平台上被问及这辆车能在哪里开时，马斯克表示，特斯拉将在得克萨斯总部修建一条环形赛道，供车主在封闭环境里体验「特技」。


不实用，不代表无价值


在看完发布会后，图灵奖得主、Meta 首席 AI 科学家杨乐昆（Yann LeCun）在社交平台上敲下了一道计算题。


他也认为，即便整车一半的重量全都分配给压缩气体，在推重比大于 1 的条件下，有用的推力大概也就维持 5 秒钟上下。


杨乐昆随后把这辆车形容成一个 700 bar 气压、600 升容积的「放屁装置」，认为它不过是一个声势浩大的营销噱头，算不上通往飞行汽车的道路。


马斯克给出的回应带着他一贯的风格——一句源自荒诞喜剧《巨蟒与圣杯》里的台词。


我朝你放个屁。

论实用，光靠喷高压气体腾空几秒，显然没法拿来日常代步。但在不少车迷和极客眼里，特斯拉这是帮他们把童年时期的脑洞搬进了现实。


在日本经典动画《高智能方程式》里，主角赛车阿斯拉达最具辨识度的配置之一，就是车身两侧的大功率风扇。


依靠这两个风扇，阿斯拉达在过弯时可以在突破抓地极限腾空跃起，在空中完成角度修正后再落回赛道。

其实在汽车工业里，琢磨风扇的并不止特斯拉一家。宝马在去年公开过一辆名为 Vision Driving Experience 的测试车，其内部的 5 台风扇能够为车身带来整整 1 吨的下压力，哪怕车辆此时完全处于静止状态。


和特斯拉 Roadster 一样，这辆车也在网上找来了一大堆冷嘲热讽。


有人调侃宝马造了一台「带四个轮子的巨型戴森吸尘器」，有人觉得 50kW 的风扇纯属浪费电，更有人觉得这套系统动静震天，除了发视频博眼球，没有任何实际意义。


▲ BMW Vision Driving Experience

但在科技演进的历史里，很多技术的价值显现往往有很长的延迟。那些今天支撑着现代社会的基础设施，刚诞生时大多也挨过类似的骂声。


最典型的例子是黄仁勋与英伟达。


2006 年，黄仁勋做出了一个让同行不解的决定：他要求英伟达出厂的每一块游戏显卡，都必须加入支持通用计算的 CUDA 架构单元。对于当时只想玩《魔兽世界》的玩家来说，这不仅不能带来画面和帧率的提升，反而让显卡变得又烫又贵。


这项被华尔街视作「毫无商业价值」的投入，一度让英伟达的股价跌去了将近八成。


直到 2012 年，Krizhevsky 和 Sutskever（后来的 OpenAI 联合创始人）用两块英伟达显卡跑出了 AlexNet 模型，大家才猛然发现，原来只有 CUDA 能搞定深度学习的大规模计算。

一夜之间，这套当年被喷成累赘的通用计算架构，成了全球 AI 开发者绕不开的刚需，也把英伟达一路推上了万亿美元市值的宝座。


难道说，黄仁勋在 2006 年就已经预见到大模型时代了？当然不可能，他当年只是觉得，物理世界纷繁复杂的模拟，迟早需要更庞大的并行计算架构。


这种技术投入在当下看往往是反常识的，因为它很难在财表里即时变现。回到汽车行业，也是一样的道理。


如果一家车企永远只挑「立刻有用」的项目去做，工程师的大部分精力，无非是围着换供后的台架测试打转，或者想方设法把车身风阻从 0.21 抠到 0.20。


这些微小的改良当然必不可少，但它们终究只是在既有的跑道里内卷。

特斯拉造出的这辆 Roadster，或许永远无法开上早高峰环路，也不可能降落在写字楼的楼顶。但光是把一辆车送上天翻个身，就已经是一道超纲的题目。为了这几秒钟，工程师只能硬着头皮，去解决那些平时造车根本碰不到的偏门问题。


马斯克自己也说，「Roadster 已经不能算是一辆真正意义上的汽车」。


正因为它不需要被当成正经车来造，反倒成了整个研发团队最没有包袱的试验场。也只有面对这种完全不考虑使用场景的项目，工程师们才有机会放开手脚，去摸一摸技术的边界。

在他们眼里，未来的家用车不一定真能飞起来，但在这个项目上积累到的经验，不会凭空消失。


技术演进向来很难按部就班，那些今天看起来毫无用处的折腾，放长远看，说不定恰恰是拉开代差的伏笔。
